Topical medicine (MFDS 200501321)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200501321. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory treatment of stiff shoulders, low back pain, neuralgia, rheumatism, bruises, sprains, muscle pain and joint pain.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory treatment of stiff shoulders, low back pain, neuralgia, rh

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200501321. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Attach it to the affected area 1 to 2 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Do not use it on infants aged 30 months or under, around the eyes, on eczema, on dermatitis caused by lacquer, on wounded areas, or on mucous membranes.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine or cosmetic (for example rash, redness, itching, dermatitis caused by lacquer), if you have an allergic constitution, if you have severe skin maceration or moisture retention, or if the user is a child, a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant, or a breast-feeding woman.
  • When using it for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Clean the affected area, wipe off sweat well, and then attach it.
  • Do not warm the attached area with a heater or an electric blanket.
  • Bathing while it is attached causes strong irritation, so remove it 30 minutes to 1 hour before bathing.
  • Also, do not attach it immediately after bathing.
  • If the symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 days of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine externally only.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • Because symptoms of poisoning may appear if a large amount is absorbed through the skin, avoid long-term use over a wide surface.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, redness with congestion, itching or pain appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for regulating the intestines through normalization of the intestinal flora and for improving diar

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201901949. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 2 packets (2 g) to 8 packets (8 g) a day, and children aged 2 years and older take 1 packet (1 g) to 4 packets (4 g) a day. Take 1 dose between meals with a drink or with milk.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, pregnant women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it for 2 days, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • To replace fluid lost through diarrhea, drink plenty of beverages containing salt or sugar.

Interactions

  • If you continue to eat while you have diarrhea, do not eat raw food, fruit, vegetables, spicy food, or frozen food or drinks.

This medicine is used for the temporary relief of a burning sensation, a feeling of irritation and discomfort caused by dry eye syndrome or by exposure to wind and sun, and for the prevention of eye irritation.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Eye drops

How it works

This medicine is used for the temporary relief of a burning sensation, a feeling of irritation and discomfort caused by

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200708107. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

When necessary, instill 1 to 2 drops into the eye that has symptoms, and discard the remaining solution and the container after instillation. When it is used at the same time as another eye drop, leave an interval of at least 15 minutes between instillations in order to avoid a dilution effect.

Precautions for use

  • Use it externally only.
  • Do not reuse it after a single use, and be sure to discard the remaining solution and the container.
  • To avoid contamination, do not let the tip of the container touch anything outside.
  • Do not use it if the color of the solution has changed or if it has become cloudy.
  • Because temporary blurring of vision may occur, be careful when driving or operating dangerous machinery until the vision becomes clear.

Possible side effects

  • If you experience pain, a change in the field of vision, or persistent redness of the eye or a feeling of irritation, or if the symptoms get worse or last for 72 hours or more, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased site) 1 time a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, and infants and children should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use it on the eyes or the area around the eyes, on mucous membranes (inside the mouth, inside the nose, the vagina), on the scrotum or external genitalia, on eczema, on diseased areas with severe moistness (dampness), skin breakdown, cracking, or injury (wounds), on the nails, or on the scalp.
  • Before using this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, patients whose diseased area is on the face or is widespread or has become purulent (festering), and patients with hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or those who have experienced it should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • Do not use it while the diseased area or the area around it is dirty.
  • Do not touch your eyes or mucous membranes with hands that have this medicine on them.
  • Be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get into the eyes, rinse immediately with cold or lukewarm water.
  • This medicine is for external use only.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, swelling, irritation, a feeling of heat, scaling, desquamation (peeling of the skin like dandruff or flakes), skin maceration, dry skin and a feeling of skin tightness, or cracking of the skin occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Who should ask first

How to apply it

After cleaning the wound area, apply a single layer, and cover it with another dressing if necessary. Changing the dressing every day is appropriate, but the frequency of use is decided according to the clinical situation.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Use it on no more than 10 % of the body surface area, and avoid contact with the eyes, middle ear, meninges, and brain.

  • Rarely, dermatitis, contact hypersensitivity, photosensitivity, and anaphylactic reactions may occur.

  • Do not use together with soap or other anionic substances, potassium iodide, or oxidizing wound cleansers.

payloads.title: Oral medicine (MFDS 201211096)
payloads.summary: This medicine is used for constipation.
payloads.content:
Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicineThis medicine is used for constipation.

Oral medicine (MFDS 201211096)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201211096. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for constipation.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for constipation.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201211096. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For the first doses, adults take 30 mL (20 g) once a day with breakfast or dinner, and in most patients, several days after the initial administration, the maintenance dose is 15 mL (10 g) once a day. The average dose for children is 0.375 mL (0.25 g) per kg of body weight per day: children aged 1 to 6 years take 3.75 to 7.5 mL (2.5 to 5 g) a day, children aged 6 to 12 years take 7.5 to 15 mL (5 to 10 g) a day, and those aged 12 to 16 years take 15 to 30 mL (10 to 20 g) a day. This medicine may be mixed with hot or cold drinks, cereal, pudding, and the like. Because the response varies from patient to patient, for patients with constipation the dose needs to be adjusted to the amount required for one bowel movement a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), abdominal pain or bleeding of unknown cause, fecal impaction, galactosemia, an ileal or rectal incision, inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, etc.), or a colostomy, and nursing mothers must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, infants, young children and children, elderly or frail people, and patients with fluid and electrolyte imbalance or chronic constipation should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • It is advisable to maintain an adequate fluid intake every day.
  • If constipation does not improve after taking it for about 1 week, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If abdominal (belly) discomfort such as flatulence, pain, abdominal pain (stomach ache), cramps, or a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, rarely vomiting, occasionally nausea, borborygmus (the sound of gas in the intestines) or anal itching, diarrhea, an increased number of bowel movements, loss of appetite, itching, elevated LDH, decreased hemoglobin, eosinophilia, or malaise occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with thiazide diuretics, corticosteroids, carbenoxolone, amphotericin B, glycosides, or alpha-glucosidase inhibitors (acarbose, voglibose).

This drug is used for the relief of pain related to the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum in adults, acute and chronic diarrhea in adults, and acute diarrhea in children aged 24 months or older.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This drug is used for the relief of pain related to the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum in adults, acute and chronic di

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200201403. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 3 g as 1 dose, 3 times a day. During the first 3 days of acute diarrhea, the daily dose may be doubled (2 times). For esophagitis, take it after meals; for other indications, take it between meals. Children aged 24 months and older take 6 to 9 g a day divided into 3 doses for 3 days, and then 6 g a day divided into 3 doses for the following 4 days. Shake the suspension well before taking it.

Precautions for use

  • Children under 24 months of age, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with severe chronic constipation, and those who have experienced intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving this medicine to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • If dehydration occurs, provide appropriate fluid replacement.

Possible side effects

  • If abdominal distension, vomiting, constipation, urticaria, rash, itching, and angioedema occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Because the drug has adsorptive properties and may affect the absorption rate or absorption time when taken together with other drugs, it is advisable to take it at an interval.

This medicine is used to relieve sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion, and watery eyes due to a head cold, allergic rhinitis, and vasomotor rhinitis.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve sneezing, runny nose, nasal congestion, and watery eyes due to a head cold, allergic rh

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 197600174. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults and children aged 12 years and older take 10 mL per dose, 3 times a day, after each meal.

Warning

  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with severe liver and kidney dysfunction, severe coronary heart disease, urination disorder, high blood pressure, or coronary artery disease, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, nursing mothers, infants aged 2 years or younger, and patients with hypersensitivity to methylparaben must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with asthma, glaucoma, arrhythmia, diabetes, or hyperthyroidism, and children under 12 years of age, should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Be careful when driving or operating machinery after taking it.

Possible side effects

  • If acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, severe skin adverse reactions (fever, erythema, numerous small pustules), high fever, sedation, drowsiness, central nervous depression, central stimulation, anxiety, sweating (perspiration), mild (slight) lowering of blood pressure, visual disturbance, mydriasis (dilated pupils), delirious speech, hallucinations, agitation, muscle cramps, rigidity (stiffness), athetosis, clonic and tonic convulsions, high fever, respiratory paralysis, coma, circulatory paralysis, skin reactions, temporary irritating pain, a burning sensation (hot feeling), thirst, nausea, vomiting, difficulty urinating (passing urine), excitement, ischemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding), or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with antihypertensives, alcohol, central nervous system depressants (hypnotics, sedatives, tranquilizers), MAO inhibitors, sympathomimetics, tricyclic antidepressants, guanethidine, bretylium, bethanidine, debrisoquine, methyldopa, sympathomimetic drugs (decongestants, appetite suppressants, amphetamine-type neurostimulants), and adrenergic blockers (inhibitors).

payloads.summary: This medicine is used for constipation.
payloads.content:
Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicineThis medicine is used for constipation.

Oral medicine (MFDS 202300045)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202300045. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for constipation.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for constipation.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202300045. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults and children aged 8 years and older take 20 to 40 ml (1 to 2 packets) a day, based on a package unit of 1 packet (20 ml). Depending on symptoms, children in particular may take 20 ml (1 packet) every other day. Dissolve 20 ml (1 packet) of this medicine in water to make 50 ml and then take it. It is recommended to take it in the morning. For children from 6 months to 7 years of age, based on a package unit of 1 packet (8 ml), children 6 months to 1 year of age take 8 ml (1 packet) a day, children 1 to 4 years of age take 8 to 16 ml (1 to 2 packets) a day, and children 4 to 7 years of age take 16 to 32 ml (2 to 4 packets) a day. If 1 packet (8 ml) a day is taken, take it in the morning; if more than 1 packet (8 ml) a day is taken, divide the dose between morning and evening. Dissolve 8 ml (1 packet) of this medicine in water to make 50 ml and then take it.

Precautions for use

  • People who are hypersensitive to this medicine and patients with inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, etc.), toxic megacolon, intestinal perforation, intestinal obstruction, intestinal stricture, or abdominal pain of unknown cause must not take this medicine.
  • Do not take this medicine for a long period without a doctor's judgment.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and older and adults take 1 dose of 2 capsules, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals, at 4-hour intervals.

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.

  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, people who have had an asthma attack when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics or cold medicines, infants under 3 months of age, people who are taking MAO inhibitors or are within 2 weeks of stopping them, and patients with genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, infants and young children under 2 years of age, those with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced drug allergy (fever, rash, redness, swelling, irritation, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver, kidney, heart, or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma, or difficulty urinating, elderly people, people who are physically weak or have a high fever, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain or with ulcer or bleeding problems, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, nursing mothers, people who smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or longer, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache, and patients with hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it 5 to 6 times, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating (passing urine), thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweats, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms with high fever, rash and redness, and burn-like blisters), asthma, liver function disorder (general listlessness, jaundice), interstitial pneumonia (with cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, rising blood pressure, headache, etc.), or myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussive (cough-stopping) expectorants (phlegm remedies), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness remedies, allergy remedies).

Category

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve all the symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202007781. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and older take 1 sachet (20 mL) as 1 dose, those aged 11 years or older and under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet (13.3 mL) as 1 dose, those aged 7 years or older and under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet (10 mL) as 1 dose, those aged 3 years or older and under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet (6.7 mL) as 1 dose, and those aged 2 years or older and under 3 years take 1/4 of a sachet (5 mL) as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) have been reported.
  • If a skin rash or other signs of a hypersensitivity reaction appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or those who have experienced it, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age (nursing infants, newborns) should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants (nursing infants, newborns) and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, children under 2 years of age, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic reactions to medicines (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating (passing urine), elderly people, people who are physically weak or have a high fever, people whose gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain persist or recur or who have ulcers or bleeding problems, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, and people with a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • When using it in a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congestion and reddening), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating (passing urine), thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or, rarely, shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling (puffiness), and chest tightness right after taking the medicine, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness (congestion and reddening) and burn-like blisters appearing on the skin over the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver dysfunction (general languor, jaundice (the skin or the whites of the eyes turn yellow), etc.), or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are within 2 weeks of stopping an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are receiving diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, etc. should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), ankylosing spondylitis, tendinitis (inflammation of the tendons), acute gout, dysmenorrhea, bursitis (inflammation of the synovial bursa), skeletal muscle disorders (sprains, contusions (bruises), trauma (wounds), lumbosacral pain (low back pain)), pain after surgery, migraine, and pain after tooth extraction (having a tooth pulled).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), ankylosing spondylitis, ten

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202402681. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis, adults take 1 to 2 packets (250 to 500 mg) per dose, 2 times a day every 12 hours. For acute gout, adults take 3 packets (750 mg) as the first dose and then 1 packet (250 mg) every 8 hours until the attack subsides. For skeletal muscle disorders, pain after surgery, pain after tooth extraction, dysmenorrhea, tendinitis (inflammation of the tendon), and bursitis, adults take 2 packets (500 mg) as the first dose and then 1 packet (250 mg) every 6 to 8 hours. Do not exceed a total daily dose of 5 packets (1,250 mg). For migraine, adults take 3 packets (750 mg) as the first dose. If necessary, an additional 1 to 2 packets (250 to 500 mg) may be taken a day, taken 30 minutes after the first dose. Do not exceed a total daily dose of 5 packets (1,250 mg). Increase or decrease the dose as appropriate according to age and symptoms. Shake the suspension well to mix it before use, then take it.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with peptic ulcer, severe blood disorders, liver disorder, cardiac insufficiency, kidney disorder or high blood pressure, patients with hypersensitivity to the ingredients of this medicine or to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as aspirin, those who have experienced asthma, rhinitis, nasal polyps, urticaria or allergic reactions caused by aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, and pregnant women (in late pregnancy) must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer or blood disorders or those who have experienced them, patients with a tendency to bleed, patients with liver disorder or a history of it, patients with kidney disorder or a history of it and patients with reduced renal blood flow, patients with impaired cardiac function, patients with high blood pressure, those who have experienced hypersensitivity, patients with bronchial asthma, patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and patients with mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), and elderly people should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely, shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure, bradycardia (slow pulse), cold sweat, swelling, etc.), PIE syndrome (pulmonary infiltration with eosinophilia: accompanied by fever, wheezing, cough and sputum), hives; sometimes rash, itching; rarely hematemesis (vomiting of blood), gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation; sometimes stomach discomfort, stomach pain, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, indigestion, heartburn, diarrhea, constipation, stomatitis (inflammation of the mouth); rarely abdominal bloating, black stools, thirst; rarely blood disorders such as agranulocytosis, eosinophilia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia (destruction of red blood cells), reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time); rarely elevated GOT and GPT values, jaundice, hepatitis; rarely renal impairment (kidney disorder), glomerulonephritis (kidney inflammation), blood in the urine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis (kidney inflammation), nephrotic syndrome, renal (kidney) papillary necrosis, protein in the urine, renal failure; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; sometimes drowsiness, impaired cognitive function; rarely dizziness, headache, numbness of the hands and feet, decreased vitality, fatigue, depression, abnormal dreams, loss of concentration, disorientation (impaired orientation), insomnia, muscle pain, muscle weakness; sometimes eczema, sweating, purpura; rarely photosensitivity, hair loss, redness (congested and reddened), necrolysis, erythema multiforme (red spots), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (skin-mucosa-eye syndrome), hives, epidermolysis bullosa, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms, fixed drug eruption, ringing in the ears, hearing impairment, visual impairment; sometimes swelling, difficulty breathing; rarely palpitations (pounding heart), myasthenia (muscle weakness), congestive heart failure, eosinophilic pneumonia, anaphylactoid reactions, menstrual disorders, chills (feeling cold and shivering) and fever, vasculitis (inflammation of the blood vessels), high blood sugar, or low blood sugar.

Interactions

  • Do not take together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (NSAIDs) or naproxen derivatives.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with hydantoin antiepileptics, sulfonamides, sulfonylurea hypoglycemic agents, propranolol and other blockers, ACE inhibitors, loop diuretics and thiazide diuretics, probenecid, aspirin, lithium, methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), zidovudine, or new quinolone antibiotics (such as enoxacin).

Apply 0.25 to 0.66 g of the cream (23 to 62 mg as lidocaine) 5 to 15 minutes before sexual intercourse. The amount and the application time differ from person to person, so use the lowest effective amount and do not use more than 2 g (184 mg as lidocaine) within 24 hours.

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to other amide-type local anesthetics, by patients with a wound or inflammation at the application site, or when the partner is pregnant.

  • Use it externally only.
  • Do not use it in the eyes or the nose.
  • It is preferable not to apply it to the same area repeatedly.

Possible side effects

  • If a rash or irritation appears in the user or in the partner, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain due to a cold, low back pain, dysmenorrhea, post-operative pain and ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion), and non-articular rheumatic diseases (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint diseas

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199804309. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 1/2 tablet to 1.5 tablets (200 to 600 mg) per dose 3 to 4 times a day, up to a maximum of 3200 mg a day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight a day, divided into 3 to 4 doses; for mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults take 1/2 tablet to 1 tablet (200 to 400 mg) per dose 3 to 4 times a day. Children aged 11 to 14 years take 200 to 250 mg per dose, children aged 7 to 10 years take 150 to 200 mg per dose, children aged 3 to 6 years take 100 to 150 mg per dose, and children aged 1 to 2 years take 50 to 100 mg per dose, orally 3 to 4 times a day. For children weighing less than 30 kg the daily amount must not exceed 500 mg, and it is preferable to avoid taking it on an empty stomach. Do not take more than the recommended amount.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients who have cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) and need to take high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients who have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding, by patients with severe blood abnormality, severe liver impairment, severe renal impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure, by patients who have or have had bronchial asthma, by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors), by patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, by pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, by patients taking high-dose methotrexate as anticancer therapy, or by patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has or has had blood abnormality, has a bleeding tendency, has or has had cirrhosis or liver impairment, has or has had renal impairment, has cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, high blood pressure, a history of hypersensitivity, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, is elderly or a child, is a pregnant woman or a breast-feeding woman, or is taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.
  • Without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: symptoms of shock (heartburn, chills, difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure); blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, hematemesis, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, oral ulcer, constipation and black stools; mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reaction, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis and acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, hepatic dysfunction such as increases in GOT, GPT and ALP, and liver impairment; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reaction, asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura, rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbance such as a blind area of the visual field, hearing loss, tinnitus and abnormal taste; vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (symptoms such as severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, oliguria, hematuria, proteinuria, increases in BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath and languor; and, at an unknown frequency, Conn's syndrome, periorbital swelling, facial swelling, malaise, fever, nosebleed and peripheral edema.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, low-dose aspirin, or high-dose methotrexate.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.

payloads.content:

Oral medicine (MFDS 201603416)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201603416. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction, and unstable angina, to inhibit thrombus formation after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA), and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (patients with multiple risk factors such as a family history of ischemic heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, obesity, and diabetes).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to inhibit thrombus formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction, and unstable angina,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201603416. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 1 tablet as 1 dose, 1 time a day. Since this medicine is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to other salicylate preparations, analgesics, anti-inflammatory agents or antirheumatic agents, patients with peptic ulcer or aspirin-induced asthma or a history of it, patients with hemophilia, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency or a tendency to bleed, patients receiving concomitant methotrexate at doses of 15 mg or more per week (15 mg/week), and pregnant women in the third trimester must not take this medicine.
  • Do not take this medicine during the first and second trimesters of pregnancy unless it is absolutely necessary.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with kidney disorder, cardiovascular circulatory dysfunction (renal vascular disease, congestive heart failure, fluid depletion, major surgery, sepsis or major bleeding events, etc.), liver disorder, impaired cardiac function or bronchial asthma, patients before surgery, young children aged 3 years or under, elderly people, patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, patients with Reye's syndrome, patients aged 14 years or under with chickenpox or influenza infection, and patients with gout should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because there is a risk of bleeding, tell your doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are going to have surgery (including dental surgery).
  • Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (e.g. difficulty breathing, generalized flushing, angioedema, hives), asthma attacks, hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, nasal congestion, cardiac and respiratory disorders, and sometimes rash, swelling, hives, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis), rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, rarely aplastic anemia, anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), ringing in the ears, deafness, dizziness, headache, agitation, rarely liver disorder, or very rarely temporary liver damage, renal impairment, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, an excessive drop in body temperature, collapse, or coldness of the limbs occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, and vomiting may occur.

Interactions

  • Other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics and salicylate preparations, and methotrexate at doses of 15 mg or more per week (15 mg/week), must not be used together with this medicine, because concomitant use may increase bleeding or reduce kidney function.
  • People taking anticoagulants, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen and naproxen, thrombolytics, other platelet aggregation inhibitors, hemostatics, antidiabetic agents (insulin preparations, tolbutamide, etc.), uricosuric agents (benzbromarone, probenecid), thiazide diuretics, lithium preparations, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, digoxin, systemically acting adrenocortical hormone preparations (excluding hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors, or valproic acid preparations should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not mix this medicine with alkaline preparations (for example, sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate) or with preparations that easily absorb moisture.
  • Concomitant use with alcohol increases damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa, and the synergistic effect of this medicine and alcohol may prolong bleeding time.

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for cough and phlegm.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202204501. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and older take 20 mL at a time, 3 times a day, at intervals of about 4 hours.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it and infants under 3 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, itching, etc.), people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure, elderly people, people with a weak constitution or a high fever, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, children under 2 years of age, people under the treatment of a doctor or dentist, and patients with cough (cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, cough with excessive phlegm, cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, chronic cough, or cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), other antitussive expectorants, cold remedies, oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness remedies, allergy remedies), or sedatives.
  • People within 2 weeks of stopping MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) must not take this medicine.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

payloads.title: Topical medicine (MFDS 200713763)
payloads.summary: This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of the surgeon's hands and arms and for the sterilization a
payloads.content:
Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicineThis medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of the surgeon's hands and arms and for the sterilization a

Topical medicine (MFDS 200713763)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200713763. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of the surgeon's hands and arms and for the sterilization and disinfection of the surgical site.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of the surgeon's hands and arms and for the sterilization a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200713763. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For sterilizing and disinfecting the hands and arms of the surgeon, put 5 mL of this medicine on the hands and arms, rub it in well for about 5 minutes to produce plenty of lather, and then rinse it off thoroughly with running water. For sterilizing and disinfecting the surgical site, apply this medicine directly or use an appropriate amount, rub it in well to produce plenty of lather, and then wipe it off with sterile gauze.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure, dermatitis herpetiformis, by patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment, or by newborns and infants under 6 months of age.
  • Before using this medicine, patients in a serious condition (burn patients, etc.), patients with a thyroid disease, patients who have had renal failure, and a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant and a breast-feeding woman should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it for the eyes or internally.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations for use.
  • Because soaps weaken the germicidal action of this medicine, wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When it is used on a severe wound, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent, and do not use tap water or purified water.

Possible side effects

  • If symptoms of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, itching, swelling, heartburn and at the same time pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, shortness of breath, etc.) or iododerma rarely appear, if pain, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness or dermatitis occasionally appears, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium preparations, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound healing preparations.

This medicine is used for disinfecting the patient's skin before surgery and for disinfecting the patient's skin before the insertion of a syringe needle or catheter.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfecting the patient's skin before surgery and for disinfecting the patient's skin before

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201402375. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply it to the area to be disinfected.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine and infants aged 2 months or younger must not use it.
  • Do not use it to disinfect surgical instruments, or on the brain, spinal cord, eyes, ears (inner ear, middle ear, outer ear), or mucous membranes (especially genital mucous membranes).
  • Before using this medicine, patients with an allergic constitution and those applying it to broken skin (especially burns), mucous membranes, or large areas of immature skin should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only; do not take it by mouth or inject it.
  • Be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it does, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.
  • Soap weakens the germicidal action of this medicine, so wash it off thoroughly before use.
  • This medicine is adsorbed by fibers and cloth (cotton, gauze, wool, rayon, etc.), so when it is used soaked into such materials, supply fresh solution if the concentration is no longer above the effective level.
  • It is a flammable liquid, so be careful.
  • Dry it before using electrical devices.

Possible side effects

  • If hypersensitivity symptoms such as local allergy, systemic allergy, contact eczema, photosensitization, shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, tightness in the chest, difficulty breathing, redness), or occasionally rash or urticaria occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used as supportive therapy for symptoms of mental and physical asthenia and as supportive therapy during the recovery period (a state of amino acid deficiency).

Category

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202204085. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adolescents aged 12 years and over and adults take 5 g once a day as L-aspartic acid-L-arginine. It is preferable to take it in the morning, but it may also be taken before bedtime. Take it with a small amount of water.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with severe renal dysfunction or hepatic dysfunction, or by patients who have or have had myocardial infarction.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has a problem with urinary retention (urine collecting in the bladder), is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, is taking it continuously for 15 days or more, or has or has had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to caramel.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.

Possible side effects

  • If diarrhea, nausea, vomiting or an allergic reaction appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with an antipsychotic or a sleeping pill.

Eye drops (MFDS 202107694)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202107694. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for the temporary relief of a burning sensation, irritation, and discomfort caused by dry eye syndrome or by wind and sun, and for the prevention of eye irritation.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Eye drops

How it works

This medicine is used for the temporary relief of a burning sensation, irritation, and discomfort caused by dry eye synd

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202107694. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

As needed, instill 1 to 2 drops into the affected eye, and after instillation discard the remaining solution and the container. When using it at the same time as other eye drops, instill them at least 15 minutes apart to avoid a dilution effect.

Precautions for use

  • Use it externally only.
  • Do not reuse it after a single use, and be sure to discard the remaining solution and the container.
  • To avoid contamination, do not let the tip of the container touch any outside surface.
  • Do not use it if the color of the solution has changed or if it has become cloudy.
  • Do not use a product whose expiry date has passed.
  • Temporary blurring of vision may occur, so be careful when driving or operating dangerous machinery until your vision becomes clear.

Possible side effects

  • If you experience pain, changes in vision, or persistent redness or irritation of the eye, or if symptoms worsen or last for more than 72 hours, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used to prevent and relieve dizziness, vomiting, headache, and similar symptoms caused by motion sickness.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to prevent and relieve dizziness, vomiting, headache, and similar symptoms caused by motion sickne

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201606763. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and older take 12 mL (2 packets) at a time, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 8 mL (11/3 packets) at a time, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 6 mL (1 packet) at a time, and those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 4 mL (2/3 packet) at a time. To prevent motion sickness, take 1 dose 30 minutes before boarding. If an additional dose is needed, take 1 dose at an interval of 4 hours or more, and limit the number of doses to 3 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Breastfeeding women and infants and young children under 3 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients who have had allergic symptoms caused by medicines, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, and patients suffering from glaucoma, urinary difficulty, or respiratory diseases such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving this medicine to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • If you use only part of 1 sachet and keep the rest, seal the opening well and use it within 2 days.

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis, emphysema, upper respiratory tract inflammation (pharyngitis and laryngitis), lung abscess, pneumonia, cystic fibrosis and postoperative pulmonary complications, and for the preparation and aftercare of bronchography, bronchoscopy, lung cancer cytology and tracheostomy.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 198600267. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

This medicine may be diluted to a lower concentration with sodium chloride solution for injection, sodium chloride solution for inhalation, sterile distilled water for injection or sterile distilled water for inhalation. For nebulization therapy using a face mask, a mouthpiece or a tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a nebulization tent or an inhaler (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases, and it is used individually according to the personal needs of the patient and the convenience of the method of administration. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes as much as about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be an amount that can maintain a very dense mist-like state inside the tent or the inhaler during the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous administration over a long period is preferable. For direct instillation, give 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the regular treatment of a patient who has had a tracheostomy, give 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When a small plastic catheter is inserted into the trachea under local anesthesia through a direct incision to give it directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree, give 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. When it is given using a percutaneous intrabronchial catheter, give 1 to 2 mL of this medicine every 1 to 4 hours with a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, give 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times by nebulization or by intrabronchial instillation before the bronchography is performed.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, is a child, or is elderly.
  • Do not use it as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • If bronchial obstruction, bronchospasm, rash or difficulty breathing occasionally appears, or if anaphylaxis rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • A slight odor (smell of sulfur) may appear, nausea, vomiting and loss of appetite may occasionally appear, and bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of pressure in the chest and irritation of the trachea and bronchi may rarely appear.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when it is used together with an antibiotic, tetracycline, erythromycin, bromhexine or the like.

This medicine is used as an adjunct to creams or solutions for skin fungal infections caused by dermatophytes, yeasts, molds and other fungi (ringworm, cutaneous candidiasis, tinea versicolor), for skin diseases with superinfection by these fungi, and for erythrasma caused by Corynebacterium, and it is used in particular to prevent reinfection in infections such as athlete's foot.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used as an adjunct to creams or solutions for skin fungal infections caused by dermatophytes, yeasts, m

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200008588. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the infected skin 2 to 3 times a day, depending on the size of the affected area and the amount of exudate. This medicine may be used alternately with a cream or a solution. In the case of athlete's foot, it is advisable to spray it on shoes and socks to dry up moisture and prevent reinfection. The treatment period varies according to the severity and location of the disease. In general, it is used for 3 to 4 weeks for fungal skin infections, 1 to 3 weeks for tinea versicolor, 2 to 4 weeks for erythrasma, and 1 to 2 weeks for candidal perineal inflammation. Use it regularly for a sufficient period to obtain the full therapeutic effect. If mycological cure has not been achieved, treatment is generally continued for about 2 more weeks after all symptoms have disappeared.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to imidazole derivatives, or those who have experienced it, must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not use occlusive dressings or wrapping unless directed by a doctor.
  • Change towels, clothes, socks and other items that come into contact with the affected area every day.
  • Before using this medicine, wash the affected area so that skin flakes are removed, make sure no moisture remains, and in particular dry the areas between the toes affected by athlete's foot completely.

  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with antitussive expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness remedies, allergy remedies).

  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.

  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

After drying the hair and scalp completely, apply 0.5 to 1 mL of this medicine only to the affected area, 2 times a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months, and do not let the total daily dose exceed 2 mL.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients under 18 years of age, patients with cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, heart valve disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), hair loss without a genetic cause, sudden patchy hair loss, abnormalities of the scalp (erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain, psoriasis, sunburn), hair loss of unknown cause, patients who have shaved the scalp, and patients with myocardial infarction or a history of it must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, elderly people should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Even if you forget to use this medicine, do not make up for the missed dose; simply apply the next dose as usual.
  • Use this medicine for external use only and do not use it on areas other than the scalp.
  • Do not use occlusive dressings.
  • This medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it comes into contact with sensitive areas such as the eyes, broken skin or mucous membranes, rinse immediately with clean water.
  • Wash your hands thoroughly after using this medicine.
  • Use hair styling products only after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, apply it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up drying.

  • If itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, hypertrichosis in areas other than where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including burning sensation and skin eruption, peeling, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormalities, occasionally diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, changes in blood pressure, changes in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in patients with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (such as polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, generalized erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), taste changes, visual impairment, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area several times in 1 day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, newborns and infants under 6 months of age, patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure or dermatitis herpetiformis, and patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment must not use this medicine.

  • Do not mix it with other preparations.

  • If difficulty breathing, flushing, hives, or iododerma rarely occurs, if pain, itching, an irritated feeling, rash, redness, or dermatitis sometimes occurs, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis, or skin discoloration rarely occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.

People aged 15 years and older take 20 mL as 1 dose, those aged 11 years or older and under 15 years take 13.3 mL as 1 dose, those aged 7 years or older and under 11 years take 10 mL as 1 dose, those aged 3 years or older and under 7 years take 6.7 mL as 1 dose, and those aged 2 years or older and under 3 years take 5 mL as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.   • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have been in the past, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is strictly necessary; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; if you are elderly or frail; if you have an allergic constitution or have experienced allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); or if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), difficulty urinating, high fever, stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, ulcer or bleeding problems, smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema (swelling), difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness right after taking the medicine, together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms accompanied by high fever, with rash and redness and burn-like blisters appearing on the skin over the whole body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, general languor, jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by coughing, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, and fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are within 2 weeks of stopping MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) must not take this medicine.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.
