Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 196400089. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For the large pills, take 1 to 2 pills per dose, 3 times a day, after meals with a small amount of water. For the small pills, take 8 to 16 pills per dose, 3 times a day, after meals with a small amount of water.

Precautions for use

  • Children aged 7 years or younger must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with high blood pressure, elderly people, patients with heart or kidney impairment, and people with swelling should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • If urine volume decreases, the face, hands and feet swell, the eyelids feel heavy, the hands become stiff, blood pressure rises, or headache or myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis, etc.) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • People who are taking potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, ethacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Oral medicine (MFDS 200000744)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200000744. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, co

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200000744. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and over and adults take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times a day, within 30 minutes after a meal.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity to this medicine, by people who have had an asthma attack after taking this medicine, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold remedy, by children under 2 years of age and infants under 3 months of age, or by patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is strictly necessary, is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, develops symptoms of ischemic colitis related to the pseudoephedrine component (for example sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, etc.), has an allergic constitution, has experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), has a liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain, dim vision, etc.) or difficulty urinating, is elderly, is physically weak or has a high fever, has persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or has an ulcer or a bleeding problem, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, smokes, has asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, has a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts for 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache, or has or has had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5 (Sunset Yellow FCF) or Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine).
  • If the symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Because drowsiness may appear after taking it, take care when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia or high anion gap metabolic acidosis appears, if symptoms of shock rarely appear (urticaria, swelling and a feeling of tightness in the chest right after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), or if asthma, generalized languor, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), pseudoaldosteronism (reduced urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiffening of the hands, a rise in blood pressure or headache, etc.) or myopathy (languor, cramp of the limbs, paralysis) appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with antitussives (medicines that stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, oral medicines containing an antihistamine (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, allergy medicines), or flucloxacillin.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinson drugs, etc.) or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one should not take this medicine.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant, alcohol, a potassium-containing preparation, a licorice-containing preparation, a preparation containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, a loop diuretic (furosemide, ethacrynic acid) or a thiazide diuretic (trichlormethiazide).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

This medicine is used for the temporary relief of itching of the eyes, watery eyes, runny nose, itching of the nose or the throat, sneezing, nasal congestion and sinus congestion.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for the temporary relief of itching of the eyes, watery eyes, runny nose, itching of the nose or t

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201706946. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 12 years and older and adults take 4 sachets (20 mL) at a time, those aged 6 years to under 12 years take 2 sachets (10 mL) at a time, and those aged 2 years to under 6 years take 1 sachet (5 mL) at a time, every 4-6 hours, not exceeding 4 doses in 24 hours.

Warning

  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children and people with heart disease, high blood pressure, thyroid disease, diabetes, glaucoma, or a breathing disorder such as asthma or chronic bronchitis should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve within 7 days, or if a fever develops, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, fever, erythema, numerous small pustules, marked drowsiness, excitement, anxiety, dizziness, insomnia, fever, or sore throat lasting 2 days or longer occurs, or if headache, fever, rash, nausea, vomiting, or ischemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance, etc.) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (some drugs used to treat depression, mental and emotional disorders, and Parkinson's disease).
  • People who are within 2 weeks of stopping a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (some drugs used to treat depression, mental and emotional disorders, and Parkinson's disease) must not take this medicine.
  • If you take sedatives or tranquilizers together with it, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for disinfecting the patient's skin before surgery and for disinfecting the patient's skin before the insertion of a syringe needle or catheter.

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfecting the patient's skin before surgery and for disinfecting the patient's skin before

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201402375. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply it to the area to be disinfected.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine and infants aged 2 months or younger must not use it.
  • Do not use it to disinfect surgical instruments, or on the brain, spinal cord, eyes, ears (inner ear, middle ear, outer ear), or mucous membranes (especially genital mucous membranes).
  • Before using this medicine, patients with an allergic constitution and those applying it to broken skin (especially burns), mucous membranes, or large areas of immature skin should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only; do not take it by mouth or inject it.
  • Be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it does, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.
  • Soap weakens the germicidal action of this medicine, so wash it off thoroughly before use.
  • This medicine is adsorbed by fibers and cloth (cotton, gauze, wool, rayon, etc.), so when it is used soaked into such materials, supply fresh solution if the concentration is no longer above the effective level.
  • It is a flammable liquid, so be careful.
  • Dry it before using electrical devices.

Possible side effects

  • If hypersensitivity symptoms such as local allergy, systemic allergy, contact eczema, photosensitization, shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, tightness in the chest, difficulty breathing, redness), or occasionally rash or urticaria occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for dryness of the eye (discomfort, stinging pain, irritation) or eye fatigue caused by wind, smoke, pollution, dust, dry heat, air conditioning, air travel, or long hours of computer use.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Eye drops

How it works

This medicine is used for dryness of the eye (discomfort, stinging pain, irritation) or eye fatigue caused by wind, smok

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202100747. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

As needed, instill 1 drop into each eye at a time, several times a day. Gently pull the lower eyelid down and, while looking up, instill one drop into the lower conjunctival sac.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with severe eye pain, patients who have experienced allergic reactions to eye drops (redness of the eye, itching, swelling, rash, congestion and reddening, etc.), and patients with glaucoma should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If the symptoms become worse or last for 3 days or more, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only.
  • Wash your hands thoroughly before use.
  • In the case of single-use products, discard the first 1 to 2 drops without instilling them when first using it.
  • This is to remove any container fragments produced when opening it.
  • Since it is a single-use preparation, use it only 1 time after opening, and discard the remaining solution and the container after instillation.
  • If the tip of the container touches the eyelid or eyelashes, the solution may become contaminated or cloudy from eye mucus or mold, so be careful, and do not use it if it has become cloudy.
  • To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others as far as possible.
  • This medicine can be used even while wearing contact lenses.

Possible side effects

  • If eye irritation rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • When using this medicine at the same time as other eye drops, instill this medicine about 10 minutes after using the other eye drops.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302160. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

After washing the face with soap or the like, apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (the diseased site) several times per 1 day.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, and women in the 3rd trimester of pregnancy, must not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women (in the 1st and 2nd trimesters, only when absolutely necessary), people who are under a doctor's treatment, those who have experienced an allergic reaction to medicines or cosmetics, and people with severe wetness or rawness should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it only on the areas with acne or pimples, and do not use it on large surrounding areas, on or around the eyes, on deep wounds, or on severe burns.
  • Be careful not to let it get into the eyes.
  • If it does get into the eyes, rinse immediately with water or lukewarm water, and if the irritation persists, consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine externally only.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Be careful not to let it touch skin other than the area of application.
  • If you take this medicine by mistake, consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If local skin irritation (e.g., rash (congestion and reddening), itching, dryness, a burning sensation (hot feeling), a stinging sensation (prickling), or swelling) occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If no improvement in symptoms appears, stop using it and consult a pharmacist or doctor.

How to apply it

After the hair and the scalp are completely dry, apply 0.5 to 1 mL of this medicine to the affected area only, twice a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months, and do not let the total daily amount exceed 2 mL.

  • This medicine must not be used by women, people under 18 years of age, patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with a cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, valvular heart disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), patients who have no hereditary factor for hair loss, patients with sudden patchy hair loss, patients with a scalp abnormality such as erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain of the scalp, psoriasis or sunburn, patients with hair loss of unknown cause, patients who are using another medicine for the scalp, patients who have shaved the scalp, or patients who tolerate the 2 % strength poorly.

  • Use this medicine externally only and do not use it on any area other than the scalp.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing.
  • Because this medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it touches a sensitive area such as the eyes, broken skin or a mucous membrane, rinse it off immediately with clean water.
  • Use hair styling products after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, use it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up its drying.

  • If any of the following appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, excessive hair growth at sites other than the area where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including a burning sensation and skin eruption, exfoliation, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormality, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, occasional diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, change in blood pressure, change in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in a person with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (including polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, systemic erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), change in taste, visual disturbance, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain.

  • Do not use it together with other medicines for the scalp, medicines that promote absorption through the skin (for example topical corticosteroids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol), or vasodilators (for example guanethidine, etc.).

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and over take 0.4 to 0.6 mL per kg of body weight per dose, at intervals of 4 to 6 hours when needed, and must not exceed 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed 25 mL a day. When the body weight is known it is more appropriate to use the amount based on body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormality, liver impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or bronchial asthma or by those who have had them, by people who have had asthma, urticaria or an allergy in response to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, by patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, or by a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has or has had peptic ulcer, blood abnormality, a bleeding tendency, liver impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or hypersensitivity, is a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, is elderly or a child, has stomach cancer, or is taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke, especially a patient with an autoimmune disease (SLE, MCTD).

  • If any of the following appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, or very rarely dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal distension and constipation; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis; jaundice and increases in GOT, GPT and AL-P; induction of an asthma attack; urticaria, eczema, purpura, occasionally rash and itching; rarely visual disturbance such as blurred or dim vision, hearing loss, tinnitus and abnormal taste; aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; fall in blood pressure, rise in blood pressure and palpitations; acute renal failure, oliguria and hematuria together with proteinuria and increases in BUN and blood creatinine; hyperkalemia, reduced urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath and languor; acute pulmonary edema; occasionally periorbital edema; and very rarely malaise, fever and nosebleed.

  • Do not use it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, diuretics, antihypertensive medicines, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, aspirin, lithium, methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin).

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with or a history of gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding, patients with severe blood disorders, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma or a history of it, patients with or a history of hypersensitivity reactions such as asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors), patients in whom pain occurs before or after coronary artery (heart artery) bypass graft surgery (CABG), pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as cancer chemotherapy, and patients with genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with or a history of blood disorders, patients with a bleeding tendency, patients with cirrhosis or with or a history of liver disorder, patients with or a history of kidney disorder, patients with cardiac insufficiency, heart disease, high blood pressure, hypersensitivity, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease, elderly people, children, pregnant women, nursing mothers, and those who have experienced hypersensitivity or allergy to Yellow No. 5 (Sunset Yellow FCF) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not take more than the recommended dose.
  • In case of an overdose, get prompt medical treatment even if there are no obvious symptoms or signs.

  • If any of the following appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: shock, anaphylactoid reaction, chest discomfort (heartburn), chills, difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure; decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, hematemesis, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, oral ulcer, constipation, black stools; mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reaction (unknown frequency), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash; hepatitis, jaundice, hepatic dysfunction such as increases in GOT, GPT and alkaline phosphatase (ALP), liver impairment; hypersensitivity, anaphylactic reaction, asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura (purple spots), rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing, wheezing; visual disturbance such as scotoma (a blind area of the visual field), hearing loss, tinnitus, abnormal taste, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness, etc.); fall in blood pressure, rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, oliguria (decreased urine), hematuria, proteinuria, increases in BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalized edema, shortness of breath, languor, periorbital edema, facial edema, malaise, fever, nosebleed, edema, peripheral edema, metabolic acidosis, loss of consciousness and convulsion.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (NSAIDs).
  • People who are taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs).
  • Do not breast-feed while taking this medicine.

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202303193. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults take 20 ml as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or those who have experienced it, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, and infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age should not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms from medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, or itching, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, children under 2 years of age when use is unavoidable, people who are physically weak or have a high fever, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma, or difficulty urinating, people whose gastrointestinal problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain persist or recur or who have ulcers or bleeding problems, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, or dizziness occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Rarely, if shock (anaphylaxis), in which urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness appear right after taking the medicine together with a pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, or mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, general languor, liver dysfunction such as jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussive expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines.
  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors used for the treatment of depression or Parkinson's disease, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping them, must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are receiving diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, or steroids should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients receiving barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.
  • This medicine contains saccharin.

Oral medicine (MFDS 201800567)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201800567. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used to reduce fever and to relieve pain caused by a cold, headache, muscle pain, menstrual pain, toothache, low back pain, and joint pain.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to reduce fever and to relieve pain caused by a cold, headache, muscle pain, menstrual pain, tooth

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201800567. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults and children aged 12 years and older take 4 tablets every 8 hours. Do not exceed 12 tablets within 24 hours.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with peptic ulcer or severe blood disorders, patients with severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder or severely reduced cardiac function, patients with aspirin-induced asthma (asthma attacks triggered by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents) or a history of it, people who have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with liver disorder or a history of it, patients with kidney disorder or a history of it, those who have experienced peptic ulcer, patients with blood disorders or a history of them, patients with a tendency to bleed, patients with impaired cardiac function, patients with bronchial asthma, elderly people, and pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Since this medicine is a sustained-release preparation, the tablet must be swallowed whole without crushing, chewing or dissolving it.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, reddening of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria, an asthma attack, etc.), thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, hemolytic anemia, methemoglobinemia, decreased platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation (a hole forming), hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, sweating, low blood pressure), rash, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), abnormal liver function such as elevated AST and elevated ALT, or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with other anti-inflammatory analgesics, other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates, or tricyclic antidepressants.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with warfarin, lithium, or thiazide diuretics.

payloads.content:

Oral medicine (MFDS 202003405)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202003405. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This drug is used for reducing fever when fever occurs due to acute upper respiratory tract infection.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This drug is used for reducing fever when fever occurs due to acute upper respiratory tract infection.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202003405. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and over take 0.4 to 0.6 mL per kg of body weight per dose, at intervals of 4 to 6 hours when needed, and must not exceed 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). For children weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed 25 mL a day. When the body weight is known it is more appropriate to use the amount based on body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood abnormality, liver impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or bronchial asthma or by those who have had them, by people who have had asthma, urticaria or an allergy in response to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, by patients being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, or by a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has or has had peptic ulcer, blood abnormality, a bleeding tendency, liver impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure or hypersensitivity, is a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, is elderly or a child, has stomach cancer, or is taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke, especially a patient with an autoimmune disease (SLE, MCTD).

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, fall in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, or very rarely dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal distension and constipation; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis; jaundice and increases in GOT, GPT and AL-P; induction of an asthma attack; urticaria, eczema, purpura, occasionally rash and itching; rarely visual disturbance such as blurred or dim vision, hearing loss, tinnitus and abnormal taste; aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; fall in blood pressure, rise in blood pressure and palpitations; acute renal failure, oliguria and hematuria together with proteinuria and increases in BUN and blood creatinine; hyperkalemia, reduced urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath and languor; acute pulmonary edema; occasionally periorbital edema; and very rarely malaise, fever and nosebleed.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, diuretics, antihypertensive medicines, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, aspirin, lithium, methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin).

This medicine is used for the temporary relief of a burning sensation, a feeling of irritation and discomfort caused by dry eye syndrome or by exposure to wind and sun, and for the prevention of eye irritation.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Eye drops

How it works

This medicine is used for the temporary relief of a burning sensation, a feeling of irritation and discomfort caused by

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200708107. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

When necessary, instill 1 to 2 drops into the eye that has symptoms, and discard the remaining solution and the container after instillation. When it is used at the same time as another eye drop, leave an interval of at least 15 minutes between instillations in order to avoid a dilution effect.

Precautions for use

  • Use it externally only.
  • Do not reuse it after a single use, and be sure to discard the remaining solution and the container.
  • To avoid contamination, do not let the tip of the container touch anything outside.
  • Do not use it if the color of the solution has changed or if it has become cloudy.
  • Because temporary blurring of vision may occur, be careful when driving or operating dangerous machinery until the vision becomes clear.

Possible side effects

  • If you experience pain, a change in the field of vision, or persistent redness of the eye or a feeling of irritation, or if the symptoms get worse or last for 72 hours or more, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for the disinfection of the hands and the skin (excluding hand disinfection of health and hygiene workers and of the surgeon during an operation, and disinfection of the skin at the surgical site).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the disinfection of the hands and the skin (excluding hand disinfection of health and hygiene

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801370. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply it to the area to be disinfected (excluding hand disinfection of health and hygiene workers and of the surgeon during an operation, and disinfection of the skin at the surgical site).

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, women who are pregnant or may be pregnant, and breast-feeding women should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use it on the mucous membrane surfaces of the brain, the spinal cord, the eyes, the ears (the inner ear, the middle ear, the outer ear), the vagina, the bladder, the mouth and the like, or on the eyes.
  • Before using this medicine, people who have experienced hypersensitivity to this medicine or an allergic reaction such as asthma and patients with an allergic constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine for external use only.
  • Since contact with the eyes may cause damage to the cornea, be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it does get in, wash it out well immediately with clean water.
  • Since soaps weaken the germicidal action of this medicine, wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • Do not use it for obstetric and gynecological purposes (disinfection of the vagina, the vulva, etc.) or for urological purposes (disinfection of the external genitalia, mucous membrane surfaces, etc.).

Possible side effects

  • If shock (nausea, discomfort, cold sweat, dizziness, a feeling of tightness, difficulty breathing, redness, etc.) rarely appears, or if hypersensitivity symptoms such as rash or urticaria, a feeling of irritation or photosensitization occasionally appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Instill 2 to 3 drops into the eye at a time, 2 to 4 times a day.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

Put 1 to 2 drops into the affected eye as needed.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, people with severe eye pain and those who have experienced allergic symptoms from eye drops such as redness of the eye, itching, swelling, or rash should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine only for instillation, that is, as a medicine put into the eye.

  • To avoid contamination of this medicine and damage to the eye, do not let the tip of the container touch the eye or any outside surface.
  • Do not use it if the color of the medicine has changed or if it has become cloudy.
  • Do not use it as a wetting solution for soft contact lenses or while wearing soft contact lenses.
  • Remove contact lenses before using this medicine.
  • Put them back on 15 minutes after instilling it in the eye.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

  • Because of its high viscosity, vision may become temporarily blurred when this medicine is instilled into the eye.

  • When this medicine is used at the same time as other eye drops, leave an interval of at least 15 minutes before using this medicine.

How to take it

Adults (aged 15 years and over) take 1 tablet per dose 3 times a day, and children aged 11 to 14 years take 1 tablet per dose twice a day, before a meal (between meals or after a meal).   • When giving it to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Eye drops

How it works

This medicine is used for allergic conjunctivitis.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200302303. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

Adults instill 1 drop at a time, 2 to 4 times a day, or as appropriate depending on the condition. For infants and children, follow the doctor's prescription.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine and children under 1 year of age should not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, people receiving allergy treatment (such as desensitization therapy), people who have experienced allergic symptoms from medicines, people with eye pain accompanied by itching or for whom it is not clear whether the symptoms are due to allergy, and pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • People who have experienced blurred vision after instillation should not drive or operate machinery until their vision becomes clear.
  • Drowsiness or a sedative effect may rarely occur after use, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 1 week or more of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only.
  • Be careful, because if the tip of the container touches the eyelid or eyelashes the solution may become contaminated or cloudy from eye discharge or mold; do not use it if it has become cloudy.
  • To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others as far as possible.
  • When using it together with other eye drops, allow an interval of at least 5 minutes between them.
  • Do not use it while wearing soft contact lenses, and put the lenses in at least 15 minutes after instillation.

Possible side effects

  • If redness, irritation, or itching of the eye persists, or if blepharitis, eyelid dermatitis, or blurring of vision occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Local irritation such as a temporary burning sensation, redness, swelling, or itching may occur.

At a glance

Category

How it works

Why this one

Who should ask first

How to take it

Adults and adolescents aged 15 years and older take 1 sachet as 1 dose, those aged 11 years or older and under 15 years take 2/3 of a sachet as 1 dose, those aged 7 years or older and under 11 years take 1/2 of a sachet as 1 dose, and those aged 3 years or older and under 7 years take 1/3 of a sachet as 1 dose, 3 to 6 times a day without water. The interval between doses should be 2 hours or more.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, people who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) or who stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks, children under 3 years of age, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine (applies to the mint flavor).
  • Before taking this medicine, people with an allergic constitution, people who have experienced allergic symptoms from medicines (e.g., fever, rash, joint pain, itching, etc.), patients with diseases such as liver disease, kidney disease, thyroid disease, or diabetes, patients with a high fever, frail people, patients with heart disease and high blood pressure, elderly people, breastfeeding women, patients with edema (swelling), patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache, and people who have experienced hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5 (applies to the mint flavor and the mint coffee flavor) should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Possible side effects

  • If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, decreased urine volume, swelling of the face and limbs, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, increased blood pressure, headache, weakness, cramps in the limbs, or paralysis occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.

  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, those who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping them must not take this medicine.

  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving this medicine to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: when violent symptoms such as rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), and burn-like blisters accompanied by high fever appear on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth and eyes), severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, fever, erythema, and numerous small pustules, asthma, general listlessness, jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout, and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200-600 mg at a time, 3-4 times a day. Up to a maximum of 3,200 mg a day may be administered. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30-40 mg per kg of body weight at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. For mild to moderate pain and colds, adults take 200-400 mg at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. Children 11 to 14 years of age take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 12.5 mL) at a time, children 7 to 10 years of age take 150 to 200 mg (7.5 to 10 mL) at a time, children 3 to 6 years of age take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 7.5 mL) at a time, and children 1 to 2 years of age take 50 to 100 mg (2.5 to 5 mL) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.
  • Patients with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid taking high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day), and patients who have cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, smoking, etc.) and need to take high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, severe blood abnormalities, severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma, patients who have experienced asthma, urticaria, or allergic reactions caused by aspirin or other anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, breastfeeding women, patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as cancer chemotherapy, and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
  • Do not take more than the recommended dose.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood abnormalities or a bleeding tendency, patients with liver cirrhosis, hepatic impairment, renal impairment, cardiac insufficiency, heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus, mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease, elderly people, children under 2 years of age, pregnant women, and patients with chickenpox should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • When taking it for a cold, take it for no more than 5 days as a rule, and without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Possible side effects

  • If shock (difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure, etc.), blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function and eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stool, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, oral ulcer, constipation, black stool, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms of unknown frequency, angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function, liver disorder, hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purple spots, visual disturbance, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever or impaired consciousness), acute renal failure, decreased urination, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and accompanying shortness of breath, listlessness, swelling around the eyes, facial swelling, malaise, fever, nosebleed, swelling, or peripheral edema occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as cancer chemotherapy should not take this medicine, and do not take this medicine together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics.
  • Before taking this medicine, people taking low-dose aspirin or ACE inhibitors and patients taking lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, low-dose methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for disinfection of the patient's skin before surgery or before insertion of a syringe needle or a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, ch

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202300393. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and older and adults take 2 capsules as 1 dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have been in the past, people who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants (newborns) under 3 months of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant (newborn) or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, etc.) related to the pseudoephedrine ingredient appear; if you have an allergic constitution or have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating; if you are elderly, frail, or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; if you have a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache); or if you have experienced hypersensitivity or allergic reactions to Yellow No. 5 (Sunset Yellow FCF).
  • If the symptoms do not improve after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, shock symptoms (hives, swelling, and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver dysfunction, or interstitial pneumonia occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance, etc.) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), antitussives (which stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are within 2 weeks of stopping an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are receiving other medicines such as diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, or steroids should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • In patients who have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol, the ability to metabolize large amounts of acetaminophen is reduced, which may increase the plasma half-life of acetaminophen.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

  • When it is used on a severe wound, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent, and do not use tap water or purified water.

Possible side effects

  • If symptoms of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, itching, swelling, heartburn and at the same time pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, shortness of breath, etc.) or iododerma rarely appear, if pain, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness or dermatitis occasionally appears, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium preparations, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound healing preparations.

payloads.title: Oral medicine (MFDS 201904193)
payloads.summary: This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (occurring at a young age), osteoarthritis
payloads.content:

Oral medicine (MFDS 201904193)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201904193. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (occurring at a young age), osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by colds, back pain, dysmenorrhea, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprains, contusions), and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (occurring at a young age), osteoarthritis

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201904193. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout, and psoriatic arthritis, adults take 200 to 600 mg at a time, 3 to 4 times a day, up to a maximum of 3200 mg per day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight per day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain and colds, adults take 200 to 400 mg at a time, children aged 11 to 14 years take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 13 mL) at a time, children aged 7 to 10 years take 150 to 200 mg (8 to 10 mL) at a time, children aged 3 to 6 years take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 8 mL) at a time, and children aged 1 to 2 years take 50 to 100 mg (3 to 5 mL) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day. For children weighing less than 30 kg, the daily dose must not exceed 500 mg (25 mL), and it is preferable to avoid taking it on an empty stomach.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic reactions, myocardial infarction and stroke, which may be fatal, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulcer and perforation may appear.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding or a history of it, patients with severe blood disorders, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe high blood pressure or bronchial asthma or a history of it, patients with hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or allergic reactions to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics (including COX-2 inhibitors) or a history of it, patients with pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG), pregnant women in the last 3 months of pregnancy, and patients receiving high-dose methotrexate as anticancer therapy must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, patients with blood disorders or a history of them, patients with a tendency to bleed, patients with liver cirrhosis, liver disorder or a history of it, patients with kidney disorder or a history of it, patients with cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, elderly people and children, pregnant women, and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: shock symptoms (chest distress (heartburn), chills, difficulty breathing, a drop in blood pressure, etc.); blood disorders such as decreased hematocrit, decreased hemoglobin, anemia, aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), and eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, hematemesis (vomiting of blood), Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), angioneurotic edema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as elevated GOT, GPT and ALP, liver disorder; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, asthma attacks, hives, eczema, purpura (purple spots), rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbances such as scotoma (an area of vision loss), hearing loss (deafness), ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, cerebrovascular accident or nervousness, aseptic meningitis or meningitis (symptoms such as severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever, or disturbance of consciousness); a drop in blood pressure, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations (pounding heart), heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, oliguria (decreased urination), blood in the urine, protein in the urine, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, decreased urine volume, generalized edema and the accompanying shortness of breath, lethargy, periorbital edema (swelling around the eyes), facial edema (swelling of the face), malaise, fever, nosebleed, swelling, and peripheral edema.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or with high-dose methotrexate used in cancer chemotherapy.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with low-dose aspirin, ACE inhibitors, lithium, furosemide and thiazide diuretics, low-dose methotrexate, coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin), or selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.
