This medicine is used for progressive keratoderma of the palms (the dry form of housewife's eczema), keratoderma of the palms and soles, ichthyosis, senile xerosis, keratosis pilaris, and atopic skin.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for progressive keratoderma of the palms (the dry form of housewife's eczema), keratoderma of the

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201905384. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

After washing the affected area, apply this medicine 1 to several times a day and then rub it in thoroughly.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with acute eczema or inflammatory skin disease, and patients with renal failure should not use this medicine, and it should not be used on mucous membranes such as the mucous membrane of the eye.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with inflammation or cracking (fissures) and patients with increased sensitivity to skin irritation should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • This medicine is for external use only.
  • Do not apply it directly to ulcers, erosions (skin breakdown), or wounds.
  • Use it carefully so that it does not come into contact with the eyes, nose, mouth, or other mucous membranes.
  • If it accidentally gets into the eyes, rinse them thoroughly with plenty of water.

Possible side effects

  • Pain, a sensation of heat, and occasionally flushing and itching may occur.
  • If hypersensitivity symptoms, occasionally eczematization, cracking (splitting) of the skin, papules, a prickling sensation, a burning sensation, or scaling, or rarely swelling or dryness occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with corticoids, dithranol, or 5-fluorouracil.

This medicine is used to supply vitamins B1, B2, B6, and C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, and reduced physical strength during or after illness (while ill or during recovery); to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders, etc.), angular cheilitis (inflammation of the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (inflammation of the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema, and dermatitis; for beriberi and eye fatigue; and to supply zinc.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to supply vitamins B1, B2, B6, and C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, and red

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201401570. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 8 years to under 12 years take 1 tablet at a time, once a day after a meal. Those aged 12 years and older and adults take 1 to 2 tablets at a time, once a day after a meal.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, nursing infants under 12 months of age, and patients with severe renal failure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hyperoxaluria; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; if the user is a premature infant or a young child; if you have cardiac and circulatory system dysfunction, renal impairment, hypoproteinemia, gout, or kidney stones; if you have experienced hypersensitivity or allergic reactions to Yellow No. 5; or if you have folic acid deficiency.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • It may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests, and it may turn the urine yellow and thereby affect clinical test values.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it for about 1 month, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loose stools, gastrointestinal disorders, digestive disorders, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary edema, red spots, asystole (cardiac arrest), or depression of central nervous system function occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with an antialdosterone agent or triamterene.
  • Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, while taking it and before and after taking it.

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased site) several times in 1 day.

Possible side effects

  • If nausea, discomfort, cold sweats, dizziness, a stuffy feeling, difficulty breathing, or redness occur rarely, or if rash or urticaria occur occasionally, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

After cleaning the wound area, apply a single layer, and cover it with another dressing if necessary. Changing the dressing every day is appropriate, but the frequency of use is decided according to the clinical situation.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.

Interactions

  • Do not use together with soap or other anionic substances, potassium iodide, or oxidizing wound cleansers.

This medicine is used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria, and itching of the skin.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticari

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202107872. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults and children aged 12 years and older take 10 mg as 1 dose, 1 time a day. Children aged 2 years or older and under 12 years take 10 mg as 1 dose, 1 time a day if they weigh 30 kg or more, and 5 mg as 1 dose, 1 time a day if they weigh less than 30 kg. Patients who are sensitive to adverse reactions should divide the dose between morning and evening. The amount may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. For the dosage in patients with renal impairment, refer to the approved product information. Pediatric patients with renal impairment require dose adjustment based on the patient's renal clearance and body weight.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, patients on dialysis with end-stage kidney disease, patients with renal failure, pregnant women and women who may be pregnant, nursing mothers, infants under 2 years of age, and patients with the rare genetic defect of fructose intolerance must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, elderly people, patients with kidney disorder or liver disorder, patients with epilepsy or a risk of seizures, and patients with predisposing factors for urinary retention such as a spinal cord lesion or an enlarged prostate should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine.
  • If you are to undergo an intradermal allergy test, stop taking this medicine 3 to 5 days before the test.

Possible side effects

  • If drowsiness, headache, vasculitis, photosensitivity, vertigo, joint pain, pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing abnormalities, or visual abnormalities occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, occasionally, malaise, numbness, asthenia, restlessness, abnormal sensations, thirst, dryness of the lips, nausea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort, diarrhea, palpitations, chest pain, leukopenia, neutropenia, lymphocytosis, eosinophilia, swelling, itching, rash, or liver function disorder with elevations of AST, ALT, GTP, ALP, total bilirubin or LDH, jaundice, hepatitis, elevated BUN, glycosuria, blood in the urine, or rarely urticaria, angioneurotic edema, fixed drug eruption, or acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take it together with theophylline or ritonavir.
  • While taking this medicine, do not take it together with a large amount of alcohol.

This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivering), fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This medicine is used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, co

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200000744. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

People aged 15 years and over and adults take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times a day, within 30 minutes after a meal.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity to this medicine, by people who have had an asthma attack after taking this medicine, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold remedy, by children under 2 years of age and infants under 3 months of age, or by patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is strictly necessary, is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, develops symptoms of ischemic colitis related to the pseudoephedrine component (for example sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, etc.), has an allergic constitution, has experienced allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), has a liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain, dim vision, etc.) or difficulty urinating, is elderly, is physically weak or has a high fever, has persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or has an ulcer or a bleeding problem, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, smokes, has asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, has a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts for 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache, or has or has had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5 (Sunset Yellow FCF) or Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine).
  • If the symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Because drowsiness may appear after taking it, take care when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, edema, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia or high anion gap metabolic acidosis appears, if symptoms of shock rarely appear (urticaria, swelling and a feeling of tightness in the chest right after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), or if asthma, generalized languor, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), pseudoaldosteronism (reduced urine volume, swelling of the face, hands and feet, heavy eyelids, stiffening of the hands, a rise in blood pressure or headache, etc.) or myopathy (languor, cramp of the limbs, paralysis) appears, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take it together with antitussives (medicines that stop coughing) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, oral medicines containing an antihistamine (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, allergy medicines), or flucloxacillin.
  • People who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinson drugs, etc.) or who are within 2 weeks of stopping one should not take this medicine.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant, alcohol, a potassium-containing preparation, a licorice-containing preparation, a preparation containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, a loop diuretic (furosemide, ethacrynic acid) or a thiazide diuretic (trichlormethiazide).
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have been in the past, people who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age, and people who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping one must not take this medicine.

  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling (edema), difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms such as rash, redness, and burn-like blisters accompanied by high fever appearing on the skin all over the body, in the mouth, or on the mucous membranes of the eyes), asthma, hepatic dysfunction (general listlessness, jaundice), interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.), pseudoaldosteronism (decreased urine volume, swelling of the face and limbs, heaviness of the eyelids, stiffening of the hands, increased blood pressure, headache, etc.), or myopathy (weakness, cramps in the limbs, paralysis) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Adults aged 15 years and over take 1 sachet (90 mL) per dose 3 times a day; children aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 sachet (about 60 mL) per dose 3 times a day; children aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1/2 sachet (about 45 mL) per dose 3 times a day; children aged 3 years to under 7 years take 1/3 sachet (about 30 mL) per dose 3 times a day; children aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/4 sachet (about 22.5 mL) per dose 3 times a day, in each case 30 minutes after a meal.   • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be taken by patients who have or have had hypersensitivity to this medicine, by people who have had an asthma attack after taking this medicine or its components, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold remedy, or by infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, is a child under 2 years of age for whom it is strictly necessary, has a constitution prone to urticaria, contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, migraine or food allergy, is a patient who has had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine, has a liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, edema, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, is elderly, is physically weak or has a high fever, has persistent or recurrent stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or a bleeding problem, is a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant or a breast-feeding woman, smokes, has asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, or has a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts for 1 week or more or recurs, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Because drowsiness may appear after taking it, take care when driving or operating machinery.
  • If the symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussive (cough-stopping) expectorants (phlegm remedies), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness remedies, allergy remedies).

This medicine is used to relieve various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202302835. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adolescents aged 15 years and older and adults take 1 packet at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. If necessary, it may be taken at bedtime. Keep the interval between doses at 4 hours.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious and potentially fatal skin reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen.
  • If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, those who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age and children under 2 years of age, and patients with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, children under 2 years of age for whom it is absolutely necessary, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, people with an allergic constitution, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, breastfeeding women, those in whom symptoms of ischemic colitis such as sudden abdominal pain or rectal bleeding related to the pseudoephedrine component appear, those who have experienced allergic symptoms caused by medicines such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching, elderly people, and people with a weak constitution or a high fever should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Before taking this medicine, people with liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric and duodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty urinating, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort and stomach pain or with ulcers or bleeding problems, and people with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, cough with excessive phlegm, cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, chronic cough, or cough accompanied by fever and rash or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If symptoms do not improve after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Drowsiness may occur while taking this medicine.
  • Avoid driving a car or operating machinery.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, (persistent or severe) thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, or insomnia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs, which may appear immediately after taking it as hives, swelling, and chest tightness together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing, or if skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, liver dysfunction such as general lethargy and jaundice, interstitial pneumonia, or symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome such as sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, or visual disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • People who are taking MAO inhibitors, which are used to treat depression and Parkinson's disease, or who are within 2 weeks of stopping them, must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, people who are receiving diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, etc. should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Patients who are receiving barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, or alcohol should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

Those aged 15 years and older take 1 packet (1,200 mg) per dose, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 packet (800 mg) per dose, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1/2 packet (600 mg), those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 1/3 packet (400 mg), and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/4 packet (300 mg), 3 times a day at intervals of 4 hours, 30 minutes after meals.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, in patients taking acetaminophen, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • People who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have been in the past, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, children under 2 years of age, and people who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping one must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have experienced allergic symptoms to medicines (e.g. fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (e.g. eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating; if you are elderly, frail, or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache.

  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis (HAGMA), rarely shock (hives, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), skin-mucosa-eye syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (accompanied by high fever, with severe symptoms such as rash and redness and burn-like blisters appearing on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver dysfunction (general lethargy, jaundice, etc.), or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with antitussives and expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when taking it together with diabetes medicines, gout medicines, arthritis medicines, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants and alcohol, or flucloxacillin.
  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202001098. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 15 years and older take 20 mL (4 packets) per dose, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 13 mL per dose, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 10 mL (2 packets) per dose, those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 6.5 mL per dose, and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 5 mL (1 packet) per dose, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Keep the interval between doses at 4 hours or more.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily amount of acetaminophen (4,000 mg).
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, those who have experienced asthma when taking other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, infants under 3 months of age, and people who are taking MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping them must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, infants and children under 15 years of age who are infected with or suspected of having chickenpox or influenza, people with an allergic constitution, those who have experienced allergic symptoms (for example, fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.), people with liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric and duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example, eye pain, blurred vision, etc.) or difficulty urinating (passing urine), elderly people, people with a weak constitution or a high fever, people with persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort and stomach pain or with ulcers or bleeding problems, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, children under 2 years of age, and patients with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, cough with excessive phlegm, cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, chronic cough, or cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving this medicine to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not take it continuously for a long period.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty urinating, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking it, together with pale complexion, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: when violent symptoms such as rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), and burn-like blisters accompanied by high fever appear on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth and eyes), severe skin adverse reactions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, fever, erythema, and numerous small pustules, asthma, general listlessness, jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia (accompanied by cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, and fever) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.), antitussives and expectorants, other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis, motion sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines).

  • Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

How to take it

Take 2 to 20 g of medicinal charcoal in 1 day, divided into several doses. In acute poisoning, administer medicinal charcoal within 30 minutes after ingestion of the poisonous substance. When the amount of poisonous substance ingested is known, the recommended dose of medicinal charcoal is usually 5-10 times the amount of the ingested poisonous substance. Increase or decrease the amount appropriately according to age and symptoms as directed by a doctor.

Warning

  • Since this medicine impairs the imaging of esophageal erosion, do not take it if a corrosive substance has been ingested.
  • Do not use this medicine in patients with diabetes without a doctor's diagnosis and prescription.

Precautions for use

  • When this medicine is used as an antidote for oral poisoning, giving medicinal charcoal together with ipecac syrup is not recommended, because the ipecac syrup is adsorbed by the medicinal charcoal and vomiting is thereby prevented.
  • If ipecac syrup and medicinal charcoal are used together, it is recommended that the medicinal charcoal be given after vomiting has been induced and completed.
  • This medicine should be given after gastric aspiration or gastric lavage has been completed with the involvement of a doctor.
  • Within 2 hours of giving medicinal charcoal, the charcoal adsorbs other medicines and therefore reduces their effect.
  • This medicine may colour the stool black.

Possible side effects

  • Indigestion may occur.

Interactions

  • Ice cream and sherbet lower the adsorptive power of medicinal charcoal, so do not take them together with this medicine.

Topical medicine (MFDS 201607113)Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201607113. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

This medicine is used for ringworm (tinea pedis, tinea manuum, tinea cruris, tinea corporis), cutaneous candidiasis, tinea versicolor, and fungal infections of the nails (fingernails and toenails).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for ringworm (tinea pedis, tinea manuum, tinea cruris, tinea corporis), cutaneous candidiasis, tin

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201607113. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

When using it for a fungal skin infection, once a day (at bedtime if possible), wipe the affected area clean, dry it completely, then apply a thin layer to the affected area and the surrounding skin and rub it in gently. When using it for a fungal nail infection (fingernails, toenails), cut the nails short and apply a thin layer once a day (at bedtime if possible) or, if necessary, twice a day (morning and evening). To prevent recurrence, continue using it for about 2 more weeks after all symptoms have disappeared.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant, nursing mothers, and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing or wrapping unless directed by a doctor.
  • In the case of candidiasis, do not use acidic soap.
  • Apply this medicine externally only.
  • Do not use it on acute inflammation or on open wound areas.
  • Be careful not to let it touch the eyes, nose, mouth, or other mucous membranes.

Possible side effects

  • Rarely, a burning sensation, a pricking sensation, dryness, erythema, itching, or local irritation may occur.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using this medicine together with other topically applied medicines.

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Those aged 8 years and older take 20 mL as 1 dose, children aged 24 months to under 8 years take 10 mL at a time, children aged 12 months to under 24 months take 5 mL at a time, and children aged 3 months to under 12 months take 3 mL at a time, 2 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine contains sodium benzoate, and benzoic acid can be a mild irritant to the skin, eyes, and mucous membranes.
  • Take this medicine by mouth only; do not use it for injection.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • It may turn the urine yellow and thereby affect clinical test values.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking it for about 1 month, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, or loose stools occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not take this medicine together with levodopa.

This medicine is used for the treatment of male-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the treatment of male-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia).

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201803770. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

After the hair and the scalp are completely dry, apply 0.5 to 1 mL of this medicine to the affected area only, twice a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months, and do not let the total daily amount exceed 2 mL.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by women, people under 18 years of age, patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with a cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, valvular heart disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), patients who have no hereditary factor for hair loss, patients with sudden patchy hair loss, patients with a scalp abnormality such as erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain of the scalp, psoriasis or sunburn, patients with hair loss of unknown cause, patients who are using another medicine for the scalp, patients who have shaved the scalp, or patients who tolerate the 2 % strength poorly.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is elderly, has edema, has thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism), has local exfoliation, dermatitis, psoriasis of the scalp or a severe burn, or has a history of heart disease.
  • Use this medicine externally only and do not use it on any area other than the scalp.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing.
  • Because this medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it touches a sensitive area such as the eyes, broken skin or a mucous membrane, rinse it off immediately with clean water.
  • Use hair styling products after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, use it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up its drying.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, excessive hair growth at sites other than the area where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including a burning sensation and skin eruption, exfoliation, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormality, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, occasional diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, change in blood pressure, change in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in a person with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (including polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, systemic erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), change in taste, visual disturbance, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain.

Interactions

  • Do not use it together with other medicines for the scalp, medicines that promote absorption through the skin (for example topical corticosteroids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol), or vasodilators (for example guanethidine, etc.).

This medicine is used for dryness and fatigue of the eyes with discomfort, a stinging pain or irritation caused by wind, smoke, pollution, dust, dry heat, air conditioning, air travel, long hours of computer use and the like.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Eye drops

How it works

This medicine is used for dryness and fatigue of the eyes with discomfort, a stinging pain or irritation caused by wind,

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202400680. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

When necessary, put 1 drop at a time into each eye, several times a day. When you put it into the eye, gently pull the lower eyelid down and put one drop into the lower conjunctival sac while looking upward.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user has severe eye pain, has glaucoma, or has experienced allergic symptoms caused by eye drops, such as redness of the eye, itching, swelling or rash.
  • Use this medicine only as eye drops, that is, only as a medicine to be put into the eye.
  • If the symptoms worsen or last for 3 days or more, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Wash the hands thoroughly before use.
  • When using a single-use product for the first time, discard the first 1 to 2 drops without instilling them, in order to remove any fragments of the container that may be produced when it is opened.
  • After opening, use a single-use product only once and discard the remaining solution and the container, and use a preservative-free multi-use product for up to 4 weeks only.
  • Do not let the tip of the container touch the eyelid or the eyelashes.
  • If it does, the solution may become contaminated or cloudy from eye mucus, mold and the like.
  • Also, do not use the medicine if it has become cloudy.
  • To prevent contamination, do not share it with others.
  • This medicine can be used even while contact lenses are being worn.
  • Follow the prescribed directions and amounts.

Possible side effects

  • If eye irritation rarely appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • When you use this medicine at the same time as another eye drop, use the other eye drop first and use this medicine about 10 minutes later.

This drug is used for reducing fever when fever occurs due to acute upper respiratory tract infection.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Oral medicine

How it works

This drug is used for reducing fever when fever occurs due to acute upper respiratory tract infection.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200608160. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Children aged 6 months and older take 0.4 to 0.6 mL/kg (5 to 7 mg/kg) per dose as needed at intervals of 4 to 6 hours, not exceeding a maximum of 4 doses a day (28 mg/kg). If the body weight is known, it is more appropriate to take the dose based on body weight, so refer to the approved product information for the recommended doses by age group.

Warning

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
  • Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and potentially fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction, and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation may occur.
  • Taking this medicine may cause serious and potentially fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration, and perforation.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, peptic ulcer, severe blood disorders, severe liver disorder, severe kidney disorder, severe heart failure, severe high blood pressure, or bronchial asthma or a history of it, patients with or a history of asthma, urticaria, or allergy caused by aspirin or other anti-inflammatory analgesics, patients being treated for pain before or after coronary artery bypass surgery, and pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and nursing mothers must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, those with a history of peptic ulcer, patients with or a history of blood disorders, patients with a bleeding tendency, patients with or a history of liver disorder or kidney disorder, patients with heart failure, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus, mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis, or Crohn's disease, elderly people and children, patients with stomach cancer, and people taking low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke should consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Possible side effects

  • If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist: rarely shock (chills, difficulty breathing, drop in blood pressure, etc.), aplastic anemia, hemolytic anemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), eosinophilia, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stool, gastritis, pancreatitis; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhea, stomach discomfort; very rarely dry mouth, stomatitis, abdominal bloating, constipation, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or Lyell's syndrome (toxic epidermal necrolysis); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, jaundice, elevated GOT, GPT and AL-P, induction of asthma attacks, urticaria, eczema, purpura; occasionally rash, itching, visual disturbances such as misty vision and dimmed vision, hearing loss, tinnitus, taste disturbance, aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, stiff neck, fever, or impaired consciousness), autoimmune diseases (SLE, MCTD); rarely drop in blood pressure, rise in blood pressure, palpitations; rarely acute renal failure (oliguria, hematuria, proteinuria, elevated BUN and blood creatinine, hyperkalemia, decreased urine volume, generalized edema, shortness of breath, listlessness), heart failure, Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency, occasionally periorbital edema, and very rarely malaise, fever, or nosebleed.

Interactions

  • Do not use together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, aspirin, or high-dose methotrexate.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with glucocorticoids, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, sulfonylureas, diuretics, antihypertensives, ACE inhibitors, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, or coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin).

Category

How it works

This medicine is used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticari

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202107872. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to take it

Adults and children aged 12 years and older take 10 mg as 1 dose, 1 time a day. Children aged 2 years or older and under 12 years take 10 mg as 1 dose, 1 time a day if they weigh 30 kg or more, and 5 mg as 1 dose, 1 time a day if they weigh less than 30 kg. Patients who are sensitive to adverse reactions should divide the dose between morning and evening. The amount may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. For the dosage in patients with renal impairment, refer to the approved product information. Pediatric patients with renal impairment require dose adjustment based on the patient's renal clearance and body weight.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, patients on dialysis with end-stage kidney disease, patients with renal failure, pregnant women and women who may be pregnant, nursing mothers, infants under 2 years of age, and patients with the rare genetic defect of fructose intolerance must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, elderly people, patients with kidney disorder or liver disorder, patients with epilepsy or a risk of seizures, and patients with predisposing factors for urinary retention such as a spinal cord lesion or an enlarged prostate should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine.
  • If you are to undergo an intradermal allergy test, stop taking this medicine 3 to 5 days before the test.

Possible side effects

  • If drowsiness, headache, vasculitis, photosensitivity, vertigo, joint pain, pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing abnormalities, or visual abnormalities occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If, occasionally, malaise, numbness, asthenia, restlessness, abnormal sensations, thirst, dryness of the lips, nausea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort, diarrhea, palpitations, chest pain, leukopenia, neutropenia, lymphocytosis, eosinophilia, swelling, itching, rash, or liver function disorder with elevations of AST, ALT, GTP, ALP, total bilirubin or LDH, jaundice, hepatitis, elevated BUN, glycosuria, blood in the urine, or rarely urticaria, angioneurotic edema, fixed drug eruption, or acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While taking this medicine, do not take it together with theophylline or ritonavir.
  • While taking this medicine, do not take it together with a large amount of alcohol.

Those aged 15 years and older take 1 packet (1,200 mg) per dose, those aged 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 packet (800 mg) per dose, those aged 7 years to under 11 years take 1/2 packet (600 mg), those aged 3 years to under 7 years take 1/3 packet (400 mg), and those aged 2 years to under 3 years take 1/4 packet (300 mg), 3 times a day at intervals of 4 hours, 30 minutes after meals.

  • People who regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or another antipyretic analgesic.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, in patients taking acetaminophen, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported, and if a skin rash or another sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

  • Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • People who are hypersensitive to this medicine or have been in the past, people who have experienced asthma when taking this medicine or its ingredients, other antipyretic analgesics, or cold remedies, children under 2 years of age, and people who are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian drugs, etc.) or are within 2 weeks of stopping one must not take this medicine.

  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis, emphysema, upper respiratory tract inflammation (pharyngitis and laryngitis), lung abscess, pneumonia, cystic fibrosis and postoperative pulmonary complications, and for the preparation and aftercare of bronchography, bronchoscopy, lung cancer cytology and tracheostomy.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for difficulty in expectorating sputum in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, pu

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 198700683. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For nebulization therapy using a face mask, mouthpiece, or tracheostomy, nebulize 1 to 10 mL every 2 to 6 hours. The recommended amount is 3 to 5 mL nebulized 3 to 4 times a day. Nebulization therapy using a mist tent or an inhalation device (Croupette) is a method needed in special cases and is used on an individual basis according to the patient's personal needs and the convenience of the administration method. This method of administration requires a large volume of solution, and sometimes up to about 300 mL may be required for a single treatment. The recommended amount should be a volume that can maintain a very dense, fog-like state inside the tent or inhalation device throughout the treatment period. Intermittent or continuous long-term administration is desirable. For direct instillation, administer 1 to 2 mL every hour. For the routine treatment of patients who have had a tracheostomy, administer 1 to 2 mL through the tracheostomy every 1 to 4 hours. When administering directly to a specific part of the bronchial tree of the lung by inserting a small plastic catheter into the trachea under local anesthesia and a direct incision, administer 2 to 5 mL every 1 to 4 hours using a syringe connected to the catheter. For diagnostic bronchography, administer 1 to 2 mL 2 to 3 times before performing the bronchography, by nebulization or by instillation into the bronchi.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine should not use it.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, patients with bronchial asthma or accompanying respiratory insufficiency, elderly people, and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • It is not used as an injection or as eye drops.
  • After nebulization therapy the face mask may stick to the face, but it comes off easily when washed with water.

Possible side effects

  • A mild odor (sulfur smell) may occur, sometimes bronchial obstruction, bronchospasm, nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite, and rarely anaphylaxis, bloody sputum, chills, fever, runny nose, stomatitis, drowsiness, a feeling of chest pressure, or irritation of the trachea and bronchi may occur.

Interactions

  • When it is necessary to use this medicine together with an antibiotic, inhale them separately, or give the antibiotic by injection or orally.

  • People who regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks every day should consult a doctor or pharmacist before taking this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics.
  • It may cause liver damage.
  • Very rarely, serious skin reactions that can be fatal, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported; if a skin rash or other signs of hypersensitivity appear after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.
  • Do not take more than the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4000 mg).

  • Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine, people who have experienced asthma when taking the ingredients of this medicine or other antipyretic analgesics or cold remedies, and infants (newborns) under 3 months of age must not take this medicine.
  • Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant or young child under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant (nursing infant, newborn) or a child under 15 years of age who has or is suspected of having chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have experienced allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching, etc.); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastroduodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, etc.), or difficulty urinating; if you are elderly, frail, or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort, or stomach pain, or ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough accompanied by excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or recurs for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever and rash or a persistent headache.
  • If the symptoms do not improve after taking 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, rarely shock symptoms (urticaria, swelling, and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweats, and difficulty breathing), mucocutaneous ocular syndrome (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) (severe symptoms with high fever, rash and redness, and burn-like blisters appearing on the skin all over the body and on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes), asthma, liver function disorder (general listlessness, jaundice), or interstitial pneumonia (with cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever, etc.) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Do not take this medicine together with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood regulators, antiparkinsonian agents, etc.), antitussive (cough-stopping) expectorants (phlegm remedies), other cold remedies, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral preparations for rhinitis (nasal inflammation), motion sickness remedies, allergy remedies).

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Attach 1 tablet (0.025 mg) as 1 dose, 1 to 2 times a day, with the white side placed on the mucous membrane of the affected area (diseased site). The amount may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. Use this medicine in the following order.   • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine and patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or those who have experienced it, patients with an infection in the oral cavity (inside the mouth), people who have had chickenpox or measles, and elderly people should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • This medicine is a patch that adheres to the oral (inside the mouth) mucosa, so do not swallow it.
  • Be careful, because if the white side becomes wet with saliva its adhesion to the mucosa becomes poor.
  • If the mucosa of the affected area (the diseased site) is very wet with saliva or the like, the patch may not adhere, so wipe it lightly with gauze or the like beforehand and then apply it.
  • When using it in infants and young children, be careful, because after application they may peel it off with their fingers.

Possible side effects

  • If candidiasis occasionally occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with skin infections caused by bacteria (tuberculosis, syphilis, etc.), fungi (candidiasis, ringworm, etc.), viruses other than herpes simplex (shingles, chickenpox, vaccinia, etc.) or animal parasites (scabies, pubic lice, etc.), patients with seriously impaired immune systems such as bone marrow transplant patients or AIDS patients, patients with eczematous otitis externa with perforation of the eardrum, patients with ulcers (excluding Behcet's disease), patients with deep burns or frostbite of grade 2 or higher, patients with perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris or rosacea, breastfeeding women, children under 18 years of age, and patients with myocardial infarction or a history of it must not use this medicine.
  • Pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and elderly people should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it in the eyes, nose, mouth or genitals.
  • Do not use this medicine to prevent transmission to other people or to prevent recurrent herpes simplex (blister) infection.
  • Do not use this medicine as a base for diluting it or for mixing other medicines.

  • Use it only for cold sores on the lips or around the mouth.

  • If commonly a feeling of dryness or peeling of the skin, occasionally a temporary burning sensation or numbness, rarely erythema, pigmentation, inflammation, bacterial (impetigo contagiosa, folliculitis, etc.) or fungal (candidiasis, tinea, etc.) skin infections, general skin symptoms (folliculitis, boils, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, a burning sensation, rash, redness, flushing, itching, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, heat rash, miliaria, worsening of wounds, bedsores, pustulosis), or, when it is used on the eyelid skin, increased intraocular pressure or glaucoma, or blurred vision of unknown frequency occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of the surgeon's hands and arms and for the sterilization a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200612696. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For sterilizing and disinfecting the hands and arms of the surgeon, put 5 mL of this medicine on the hands and arms, rub it in well for about 5 minutes to produce plenty of lather, and then rinse it off thoroughly with running water. For sterilizing and disinfecting the surgical site, apply this medicine directly or use an appropriate amount, rub it in well to produce plenty of lather, and then wipe it off with sterile gauze.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure, or dermatitis herpetiformis, patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment, and newborns and infants under 6 months of age must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, seriously ill patients (such as burn patients), those with a history of thyroid disease or renal failure, and pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and nursing mothers should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it in the eyes or take it by mouth.
  • Be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it does, rinse immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations.
  • Soap weakens the germicidal action of this medicine, so wash it off thoroughly before use.
  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When it is used on severe wounds, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent; do not use tap water or purified water.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (difficulty breathing, flushing, hives, etc.) or iododerma rarely occur, if pain, itching, an irritated feeling, rash, redness, or dermatitis sometimes occurs, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis, or skin discoloration rarely occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium preparations, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound healing preparations.

Use 15 mL per dose, twice a day: rinse the mouth or gargle for about 1 minute and then spit it out; use it after brushing the teeth. Immediately after use, avoid rinsing with water or another mouthwash, brushing the teeth, or having food. Who should ask first

How to apply it

Spray this medicine into each nostril every 2 to 3 hours as needed. The number of sprays varies according to age. Insert the nozzle into the nostril and point its tip slightly backwards. Press the pump firmly to activate the spray, spray the specified amount into both nostrils, then tilt your head to the right for 10 seconds and then to the left for 10 seconds. After that, hold your nose with your hand to close the nostrils and bend your head forward for 10 seconds. Infants may be given 1 spray, those aged 1 month to 12 months 1 to 2 sprays, those aged 1 to 2 years 1 to 3 sprays, those aged 2 to 5 years 1 to 4 sprays, those aged 5 to 8 years 1 to 5 sprays, those aged 8 to 12 years 1 to 6 sprays, and adults 1 to 8 sprays.

  • Use this medicine only as a nasal preparation, that is, a medicine applied inside the nose.
  • One product should be used by only one person.
  • To keep the solution from running down into the larynx or pharynx, use it while lying on your side at an angle or while standing with your head tilted.

  • Be careful not to inhale the vapor.

  • If severe or persistent pain and irritation occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for the treatment of male-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the treatment of male-pattern hair loss (androgenetic alopecia).

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202100410. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

After drying the hair and scalp completely, apply 0.5 to 1 mL of this medicine only to the affected area, 2 times a day (morning and evening), for at least 4 months, and do not let the total daily dose exceed 2 mL.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, patients under 18 years of age, patients with cardiovascular disease (coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, congestive heart failure, heart valve disease, treated or untreated high blood pressure, low blood pressure), hair loss without a genetic cause, sudden patchy hair loss, abnormalities of the scalp (erythema, inflammation, infection, irritation or pain, psoriasis, sunburn), hair loss of unknown cause, patients who have shaved the scalp, and patients with myocardial infarction or a history of it must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, elderly people should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Even if you forget to use this medicine, do not make up for the missed dose; simply apply the next dose as usual.
  • Use this medicine for external use only and do not use it on areas other than the scalp.
  • Do not use occlusive dressings.
  • This medicine may cause burning and irritation of the eyes, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it comes into contact with sensitive areas such as the eyes, broken skin or mucous membranes, rinse immediately with clean water.
  • Wash your hands thoroughly after using this medicine.
  • Use hair styling products only after this medicine has dried, and when using it in the evening, apply it 2 to 4 hours before bedtime so that it can dry.
  • Because circulation of air over the scalp may reduce the effect of this medicine, do not use a hair dryer to speed up drying.

Possible side effects

  • If itching, scaling, erythema, redness, dermatitis, dry skin, hypertrichosis in areas other than where this medicine was applied (facial hair growth in women), folliculitis, local irritation including burning sensation and skin eruption, peeling, hair loss, skin abscess, acne, nail disorder, seborrhea, eczema, hair abnormalities, occasionally diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, changes in blood pressure, changes in pulse, palpitations, increased heart rate, pericardial effusion, pericarditis, embolism, tachycardia, worsening of pre-existing angina or induction of angina in patients with undiagnosed coronary artery disease, bronchitis, upper respiratory tract infection, sinusitis, difficulty breathing, shortness of breath, fracture, back pain, tendinitis, pain, neuritis (such as polyneuritis), weakness, dizziness, headache, feeling dazed, fainting, hepatitis, edema, kidney stones, inflammation and fluid retention, fever, urticaria, allergic rhinitis, generalized erythema and facial swelling, chills, eye irritation, bitter taste, otitis (especially otitis externa), taste changes, visual impairment, erectile dysfunction, stabbing pain, or sudden unexplained weight gain occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • While using this medicine, do not use it together with other scalp medicines, topical corticoids, retinoids, petrolatum, dithranol, medicines known to promote absorption through the skin, or vasodilators such as guanethidine.
