This medicine is used for dryness of the eye (discomfort, stinging pain, irritation) or eye fatigue caused by wind, smoke, pollution, dust, dry heat, air conditioning, air travel, or long hours of computer use.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Eye drops

How it works

This medicine is used for dryness of the eye (discomfort, stinging pain, irritation) or eye fatigue caused by wind, smok

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 202100747. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

As needed, instill 1 drop into each eye at a time, several times a day. Gently pull the lower eyelid down and, while looking up, instill one drop into the lower conjunctival sac.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, patients with severe eye pain, patients who have experienced allergic reactions to eye drops (redness of the eye, itching, swelling, rash, congestion and reddening, etc.), and patients with glaucoma should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • If the symptoms become worse or last for 3 days or more, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only.
  • Wash your hands thoroughly before use.
  • In the case of single-use products, discard the first 1 to 2 drops without instilling them when first using it.
  • This is to remove any container fragments produced when opening it.
  • Since it is a single-use preparation, use it only 1 time after opening, and discard the remaining solution and the container after instillation.
  • If the tip of the container touches the eyelid or eyelashes, the solution may become contaminated or cloudy from eye mucus or mold, so be careful, and do not use it if it has become cloudy.
  • To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others as far as possible.
  • This medicine can be used even while wearing contact lenses.

Possible side effects

  • If eye irritation rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • When using this medicine at the same time as other eye drops, instill this medicine about 10 minutes after using the other eye drops.

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Eye drops

How it works

This medicine is used for allergic conjunctivitis.

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200302303. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to use the eye drops

Adults instill 1 drop at a time, 2 to 4 times a day, or as appropriate depending on the condition. For infants and children, follow the doctor's prescription.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine and children under 1 year of age should not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, people receiving allergy treatment (such as desensitization therapy), people who have experienced allergic symptoms from medicines, people with eye pain accompanied by itching or for whom it is not clear whether the symptoms are due to allergy, and pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • People who have experienced blurred vision after instillation should not drive or operate machinery until their vision becomes clear.
  • Drowsiness or a sedative effect may rarely occur after use, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.
  • If there is no improvement in symptoms after 1 week or more of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only.
  • Be careful, because if the tip of the container touches the eyelid or eyelashes the solution may become contaminated or cloudy from eye discharge or mold; do not use it if it has become cloudy.
  • To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others as far as possible.
  • When using it together with other eye drops, allow an interval of at least 5 minutes between them.
  • Do not use it while wearing soft contact lenses, and put the lenses in at least 15 minutes after instillation.

Possible side effects

  • If redness, irritation, or itching of the eye persists, or if blepharitis, eyelid dermatitis, or blurring of vision occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Local irritation such as a temporary burning sensation, redness, swelling, or itching may occur.

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of the surgeon's hands and arms and for the sterilization and disinfection of the surgical site.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of the surgeon's hands and arms and for the sterilization a

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199904088. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

For sterilizing and disinfecting the hands and arms of the surgeon, put 5 mL of this medicine on the hands and arms, rub it in well for about 5 minutes to produce plenty of lather, and then rinse it off thoroughly with running water. For sterilizing and disinfecting the surgical site, apply this medicine directly or use an appropriate amount, rub it in well to produce plenty of lather, and then wipe it off with sterile gauze.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure, dermatitis herpetiformis, by patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment, or by newborns and infants under 6 months of age.
  • Before using this medicine, patients in a serious condition (burn patients, etc.), patients with a thyroid disease, patients who have had renal failure, and a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant and a breast-feeding woman should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it for the eyes or internally.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations for use.
  • Because soaps weaken the germicidal action of this medicine, wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When it is used on a severe wound, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent, and do not use tap water or purified water.

Possible side effects

  • If symptoms of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, itching, swelling, heartburn and at the same time pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, shortness of breath, etc.) or iododerma rarely appear, if pain, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness or dermatitis occasionally appears, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium preparations, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound healing preparations.

How it works

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Those aged 12 years and older and adults spray 1 spray at a time into each nostril (inside the nose), 3 times a day. Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the protective cap. When using this medicine for the first time, press the pump several times to check that the solution is sprayed evenly. Insert the spray into the nostril and press the spray firmly to deliver 1 dose (1 spray). While spraying, breathe in gently through the nose so that the solution is distributed well. Remove the spray before the pressure drops. After use, close the protective cap and store it.

Adults usually insert 1 tablet per dose deep into the vagina at bedtime, 1 time a day for 6 consecutive days. When used as short-term therapy, adults insert 2 tablets per dose deep into the vagina at bedtime, 1 time a day for 3 consecutive days.

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or a history of it, and patients with genetic problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption, must not use this medicine.

  • Do not use it orally.
  • Also, do not swallow it.
  • Do not use the applicator during pregnancy.
  • Do not use it during menstruation.
  • If vulvitis or candidal balanitis is also present, it is advisable to use a clotrimazole cream preparation in addition.
  • If symptoms such as itching or inflammation occur, the sexual partner should also receive topical treatment.
  • To prevent reinfection, change personal items such as towels and underwear every day, and boil and wash the ones that have been used.
  • While using this medicine, do not use tampons, vaginal douches, cleansers, or other products inserted into the vagina.
  • In addition, do not have vaginal intercourse.
  • Do not let this medicine come into contact with the eyes.
  • Only children aged 12 years and older and adults should use it.
  • This medicine may weaken latex or rubber products such as condoms and contraceptive diaphragms.

  • If an anaphylactic reaction, a high fever of 38 degrees Celsius or higher, angioedema, hypersensitivity, fainting, low blood pressure, difficulty breathing, abdominal pain, nausea, rash, urticaria, itching, vaginal exfoliation (peeling), vaginal discharge, vaginal bleeding and/or associated shoulder pain, vulvovaginal discomfort, vulvovaginal erythema, a vulvovaginal burning sensation, vulvovaginal itching, vulvovaginal pain, irritation at the application site, swelling, or pain occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

How it works

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 201801818. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Use this medicine in the following order. Remove the applicator from its packaging and hold it with the sponge facing downwards. Do not touch the sponge part of the applicator. Squeeze the applicator firmly only once so that the ampoule breaks and the solution comes out, and leave the broken ampoule inside the applicator. For the 26 mL product, squeeze the lever on the handle firmly, and for the other products squeeze both wings firmly. Do not squeeze or press the wings repeatedly in order to wet the sponge quickly. Press and release the sponge against the treatment area until the solution is visible on the skin, wetting the sponge and completely wetting the treatment area with the solution. For a dry surgical site (e.g. the abdomen or an arm), once the solution is visible on the skin, rub gently back and forth for 30 seconds to treat that area. For a moist surgical site (e.g. the groin fold), rub gently back and forth repeatedly for about 2 minutes. Let the area to which the solution has been applied dry completely in the air, and do not wipe the solution off. Discard the applicator after a single use, together with any remaining solution that was not used on the treatment area. It is not necessary to use the entire amount.

Precautions for use

  • People with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine, isopropanol, or Yellow No. 5 and infants aged 2 months or younger should not use this medicine.
  • Do not use this medicine for disinfecting surgical instruments, or on nervous tissue (e.g., brain or spinal cord tissue), the eyes, ears, mouth, mucous membranes, genital mucous membranes, open wounds, or torn or damaged skin, or for general washing of the skin.
  • Before using this medicine, people with hypersensitivity to other medicines, people who have experienced allergic diseases such as asthma or who have a family history of them, people with hypersensitivity to chlorhexidine preparations, and people with a drug-hypersensitive constitution should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use it externally only on intact skin.
  • Contact with the eyes may cause corneal damage, so be careful not to let it get into the eyes; if it does get in, rinse thoroughly with clean water immediately.

Possible side effects

  • If shock symptoms (nausea, malaise, cold sweat, dizziness, a stifling feeling, difficulty breathing, redness, a sudden drop in blood pressure, urticaria, angioedema, etc.), occasionally rash, photosensitization, irritation, sensitization, erythema or inflammation, itching, dry and thinly peeling skin, local pain at the application site, or local skin reactions, or very rarely rash (e.g., erythematous, papular, or maculopapular), blisters, small blisters at the application site, a burning sensation of the skin, dermatitis, eczema, chemical burns in newborns, eye irritation, congestion, impaired vision, or eye damage occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used as an adjunct to creams or solutions for skin fungal infections caused by dermatophytes, yeasts, molds and other fungi (ringworm, cutaneous candidiasis, tinea versicolor), for skin diseases with superinfection by these fungi, and for erythrasma caused by Corynebacterium, and it is used in particular to prevent reinfection in infections such as athlete's foot.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used as an adjunct to creams or solutions for skin fungal infections caused by dermatophytes, yeasts, m

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200008588. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the infected skin 2 to 3 times a day, depending on the size of the affected area and the amount of exudate. This medicine may be used alternately with a cream or a solution. In the case of athlete's foot, it is advisable to spray it on shoes and socks to dry up moisture and prevent reinfection. The treatment period varies according to the severity and location of the disease. In general, it is used for 3 to 4 weeks for fungal skin infections, 1 to 3 weeks for tinea versicolor, 2 to 4 weeks for erythrasma, and 1 to 2 weeks for candidal perineal inflammation. Use it regularly for a sufficient period to obtain the full therapeutic effect. If mycological cure has not been achieved, treatment is generally continued for about 2 more weeks after all symptoms have disappeared.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to imidazole derivatives, or those who have experienced it, must not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Use this medicine for external use only.
  • Do not use this medicine on the cornea or conjunctiva as an ophthalmic preparation.
  • Do not use occlusive dressings or wrapping unless directed by a doctor.
  • Change towels, clothes, socks and other items that come into contact with the affected area every day.
  • Before using this medicine, wash the affected area so that skin flakes are removed, make sure no moisture remains, and in particular dry the areas between the toes affected by athlete's foot completely.
  • Because Candida grows well in acidic conditions, do not use acidic soap in cases of candidiasis.

Possible side effects

  • Vascular insufficiency, anaphylactic reactions, hypersensitivity, low blood pressure, fainting, respiratory problems, difficulty breathing, herpes (blisters), contact dermatitis, erythema (red spots), paresthesia (abnormal sensation), skin peeling, itching, rash, urticaria (hives), a stinging or burning sensation of the skin, irritation at the application site, reactions at the application site, swelling, and pain may occur.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take (use) it together with amphotericin B or polyene antibiotics.

  • Do not use it for obstetric and gynecological purposes (disinfection of the vagina, the vulva, etc.) or for urological purposes (disinfection of the external genitalia, mucous membrane surfaces, etc.).

Possible side effects

  • If shock (nausea, discomfort, cold sweat, dizziness, a feeling of tightness, difficulty breathing, redness, etc.) rarely appears, or if hypersensitivity symptoms such as rash or urticaria, a feeling of irritation or photosensitization occasionally appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of torn wounds, burns and wounds, the sterilization and disinfection of ulcers and abscesses, the disinfection of infected skin surfaces, the sterilization and disinfection of surgical sites, and the disinfection of injection and catheter sites.

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the sterilization and disinfection of torn wounds, burns and wounds, the sterilization and dis

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 200713754. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (diseased site) several times a day.

Precautions for use

  • This medicine must not be used by patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, by patients with thyroid dysfunction (especially nodular goiter, endemic goiter, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, etc.), renal failure, dermatitis herpetiformis, by patients before or after radioactive iodine treatment, or by newborns and infants under 6 months of age.
  • Before using this medicine, patients in a serious condition (burn patients, etc.), patients with a thyroid disease, patients who have had renal failure, and a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant and a breast-feeding woman should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Do not use it for the eyes or internally.
  • Be careful to keep it out of the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse them immediately with clean water.
  • Do not mix it with other preparations for use.
  • Because soaps weaken the germicidal action of this medicine, wash them off thoroughly before use.
  • Wash and disinfect the affected area thoroughly.
  • When it is used on a severe wound, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent, and do not use tap water or purified water.

Possible side effects

  • If symptoms of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing, urticaria, itching, swelling, heartburn and at the same time pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, shortness of breath, etc.) or iododerma rarely appear, if pain, a feeling of irritation, rash, redness or dermatitis occasionally appears, or if a burning sensation, skin ulcer, contact dermatitis or skin discoloration rarely appears, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Do not use this medicine together with hydrogen peroxide.
  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with lithium preparations, chlorhexidine, sulfadiazine and silver compounds, alkalis, preparations containing mercury, or enzyme-based wound healing preparations.

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area (the diseased site) 1 time a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and nursing mothers, and young children and children must not use this medicine.
  • Do not use it on or around the eyes, on mucous membranes (the mouth, the inside of the nose, the vagina), on the scrotum or the vulva, on eczema, on diseased areas with severe wetness (dampness), rawness, cracking, or injury (wounds), on the nails, or on the scalp.
  • Before using this medicine, those with an allergic constitution, those whose diseased area is on the face or is extensive or suppurating (festering), and patients with hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or a history of it should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration carefully.
  • Do not use it while the diseased area or the area around it is dirty.
  • Be careful not to let it get into the eyes, and if it does get into the eyes, rinse immediately with cold or lukewarm water.
  • Use this medicine externally only.

Possible side effects

  • If rash and redness, itching, swelling, irritation, a feeling of heat, scaling, desquamation (peeling of the skin like dandruff or flakes), skin maceration, dry skin and a feeling of skin tightness, or cracking of the skin occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area 1 to 3 times a day.

Precautions for use

  • Patients with hypersensitivity to this medicine or to aminoglycoside antibiotics such as streptomycin, kanamycin, gentamicin, and neomycin, or to bacitracin, and those who have experienced it, patients with skin infections (tuberculosis, syphilis, candidiasis, ringworm, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia, scabies, pubic lice), patients with eczematous otitis externa with perforation of the eardrum, ulcers (excluding Behcet's disease), deep second-degree or more severe burns and frostbite, perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris, or rosacea should not use this medicine.
  • Before using this medicine, pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women, infants and children, and patients with hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or those who have experienced it should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Follow the prescribed dosage and administration exactly.
  • When giving it to a child, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.
  • Do not use it for the eyes.
  • Do not use it for purposes other than treatment, such as with makeup or after shaving.
  • Do not use an occlusive dressing without a doctor's supervision.

  • If impetigo contagiosa, folliculitis, viral infection, boils, skin irritation, stinging pain, fever, a burning sensation, itching, rash, redness, flushing, dry skin, pustular dermatitis, heat rash, worsening of wounds, bedsores, pustulosis, hypersensitivity, skin discoloration, hypertrichosis, acneiform eruption, hypopigmentation, perioral dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, skin maceration, 2nd (secondary) infection, skin atrophy, striae, or, when it is used on the eyelid skin, increased intraocular pressure or glaucoma (blurred vision, impaired vision) occurs, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Because of systemic absorption, reversible suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, Cushing's syndrome, hyperglycemia, diabetes, and impaired vision may occur.

This medicine is used for the following skin diseases caused by yeast fungi (dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, tinea versicolor).

At a glance

Category

Over-the-counter medicine · Topical medicine

How it works

This medicine is used for the following skin diseases caused by yeast fungi (dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, tinea vers

Why this one

Based on the official MFDS approval for product code 199202073. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the product name.

Who should ask first

If any item in the safety information applies to you, ask the pharmacist at the store first.

How to apply it

Apply this medicine to the infected area (trunk, face, scalp, hair), leave it on for 3 to 5 minutes like an ordinary shampoo, and then rinse it off. As for the treatment period: for dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis, apply 2 times a week for 2 to 4 weeks, and to prevent recurrence apply 1 time every 1 to 2 weeks; for tinea versicolor, apply 1 time a day for up to 5 days, and to prevent recurrence apply 1 time a day as a single therapy before sun exposure for up to 3 days.

Precautions for use

  • Patients who are hypersensitive to this medicine must not use it, and it must not be used on a scalp with wounds or inflammation or on areas with severe erosion.
  • Before using this medicine, women who are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding, and children should consult a doctor or pharmacist.
  • Use this medicine for external use only.
  • Do not use this medicine for the eyes; apply it carefully so that it does not touch the eyes, and if it gets into the eyes by mistake, rinse them out completely with plenty of water.

Possible side effects

  • Burns at the application site, conjunctivitis, eye irritation, increased tearing, hair loss, hypersensitivity of sensation, folliculitis, pustules, rash, tenderness, acne, hair loss, dry skin, skin disorders, abnormal hair texture, change in hair color, folliculitis, taste disturbance, and urticaria may occur.
  • If hypersensitivity symptoms or a feeling of irritation occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Interactions

  • Consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it together with antifungal medicines of the same class (miconazole, econazole, isoconazole, etc.).
